538666|2026-06.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.
538666|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.1,074 crore, with volume down 1.6% and forex contributing 12.7 points. EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin rose 120 bps to 36.7%, driven by mix in NAFTA, LATAM and rest of world. Europe revenue softened as distributors cut stock after an unusual heatwave, though Europe gross margin improved to 44.2%. Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and about 35% gross margin.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue softened as distributors cut stock after heatwave. Gross margin 44.2% vs 42.9% in Q1 FY26. Management said restocking has largely normalised.

segments.name: NAFTA
segments.commentary: Gross margin 32.8% vs 25.9% a year ago; growth strong and margins improved this quarter.

segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Among the strongest growth engines this quarter, but gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% a year ago.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Gross margin 30.8% vs 26.8% in Q1 FY26; growth reported as good with better profitability.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 10-15% maintained; volume growth expected at about 5-10%.
FY27 gross margin guided at 35% to 37% (management, in Q&A), and EBITDA margin in the 18-20% range.
Effective tax rate on annualised basis expected at 18-20%, with Q1 running higher.
Amortisation expected to be about Rs.370-375 crore annualised for FY27 vs about Rs.325 crore last year.
Management expects Europe volumes to recover to prior-year levels and the next three quarters to be better than Q1; last month of Q2 said to be better than Q1.
Registration investment of about Rs.450-500 crore per year; FY27 spend to rise further.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was Rs.273 crore against FY27 guidance of Rs.500 crore; management says guidance not revised and the year could be Rs.480-550 crore.
Q1 capex was elevated by heavy data compensation payments, which management says will not repeat.
Total product registrations at 30 June 2026 were 3,016 (3,011 at 31 March 2026), with 1,027 applications pending.
Registrations by region: Europe 1,682 (up 3), NAFTA 325 (up 2), LATAM 760 (flat), rest of world 249 (flat).
demand_pricing: Volume declined 1.6% YoY; forex added 12.7 points and product mix subtracted 2.1 points.
Management said prices are improving sequentially after a severe decline about two years ago.
Europe revenue fell on distributor destocking linked to heatwave; management attributes this to weather, not molecules.
LATAM and NAFTA growth may partly reflect customer pre-buying ahead of season, per analyst; management said there is no strong trend.
Sourcing is 100% contract manufacturing, mainly from China, and all purchases are in US dollars.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the 9% revenue growth into volume, forex and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume -1.6%, forex +12.7%, product mix -2.1%, total +9%. Management said the mix impact is concentrated in Europe and should improve next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.7.5 crore forex gain and its accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: It is mainly unrealised, from repricing foreign-currency receivables and payables at each balance sheet date. Q1 FY26 had a Rs.73 crore unrealised gain from a roughly 10% EUR/USD move. EBITDA excludes forex.

qa_highlights.question: Has Europe restocking normalised and what is FY27 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restocking has improved and is largely normal, and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex Rs.273 crore in Q1 vs Rs.500 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance not revised; Q1 included heavy data compensation spend that is not expected to recur. Full year could be Rs.480-550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report PAT excluding forex for like-to-like comparison?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO pointed to the investor presentation, which gives PBT and EBIT excluding forex. He said more clarity will be provided in future presentations.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the NAFTA and LATAM gross margin, and do margins hold for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe mix and price increases drove margins, LATAM volumes grew but margins dipped, and it expects Europe and NAFTA margins to stay in the same range.

risks_watch: Pace of Europe volume recovery after distributor destocking; management guides to a better next three quarters but gave no quantified timing.
LATAM gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% despite strong volume growth.
Forex volatility: EUR/USD near 1.14 vs about 1.16-1.17 last year; management said it cannot be predicted.
Amortisation rising to about Rs.370-375 crore annualised, which pressures reported profit.
Registration pace: about 100 new registrations over three years versus about 300 in FY21-23, per analyst; no FY27 registration target given.
Capex range wide (Rs.480-550 crore) with no firm guidance revision.
538666|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full-year outlook and on Europe recovery, but evasive on forex reporting, the capex range and the drivers of regional margins, which management called too detailed for the call. Management often deflected to weather and uncertainty.
key_quotes: It has improved and has reached to normal. In most of the cases, it is reaching the normality.
We don't manufacture anything anywhere in the world, including India.
Between 35% to 37%.
So, on annualized basis, could be around Rs. 370-375 crores.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs.73.1 crore in Q1 FY26
PBT before forex Rs.111 crore, +16% YoY
vs Rs.702 crore at 31 Mar 2026; debt-free

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin 120 bps to 36.7% in Q1; FY27 guided at EBITDA 18-20% and gross margin 35-37%, with Europe and NAFTA margins expected to hold, though Q1 EBITDA margin still sits below the 18-20% range.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 volume growth guided at about 5-10% and Europe volumes expected to return to prior-year levels, with the next three quarters better than Q1, though Q1 volume fell 1.6% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Q1 capex was Rs.273 crore against Rs.500 crore FY27 guidance, with full year at Rs.480-550 crore and no new capacity or board-level expansion plan discussed; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% was only maintained, not raised, and Q1 revenue grew 9% with volume down 1.6%, so an upgrade looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Europe volume recovery is unquantified and LATAM gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0%, while amortisation rises to Rs.370-375 crore annualised and forex gains fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore.

rows.label: Sequential price improvement
rows.why: Management said prices are improving sequentially after a severe decline about two years ago, and Europe mix and price increases drove the NAFTA and Europe margin gains.

rows.label: Working capital days at 88
rows.why: Working capital days improved 10 days QoQ to 88 and the company remains debt-free with Rs.767 crore in cash and liquid investments.

rows.label: Registration pipeline
rows.why: Registrations rose to 3,016 from 3,011 with 1,027 applications pending, but registrations are about 100 over three years vs about 300 in FY21-23 and no FY27 target was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the full-year guidance and the Europe recovery but evasive on forex reporting, the Rs.480-550 crore capex range and the regional margin drivers, while analysts pressed on LATAM margin decline, forex-driven growth and the thin registration pace.

538668|2026-03.headline: Meghna Infracon FY26 revenue rose 15.84% to INR46.2 crore, but PAT fell 4.28% as carry-over securities profits lapsed.
538668|2026-03.overview: Management described the company as transitioning from Naysaa Securities to a Mumbai-focused redevelopment developer. FY26 revenue from operations was INR46.2 crore versus INR39.88 crore, and Q4 revenue was INR18.48 crore, up 52.47% YoY. FY26 PAT was INR5.59 crore, down about 4.28% YoY, which management attributed to the absence of carry-over profits from the earlier securities business. Management guided to a sharp increase in GDV and profitability over the coming years, with current GDV pipeline stated above INR2,100 crore.

financial_highlights.change: +15.84% YoY vs INR39.88 crore in FY25
+52.47% YoY vs INR12.12 crore in Q4 FY25
Increase of about INR6.92 crore YoY as stated
Down from 29%, per analyst question; not disputed by management
Up from INR46,822 per sq ft, per analyst question

segments.name: Residential redevelopment (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Five ongoing projects including Riviera, Rivaan, Pranam (Versova), Manju Villa and Joshville (Santa Cruz); ongoing portfolio about 290,000 sq ft and INR280 crore GDV. Goregaon projects 70-80% sold.

segments.name: Commercial (Meghna One IT Park, Wagle Estate Thane)
segments.commentary: Wagle Estate commercial project, GDV INR300 crore, launch date blocked for 22 June 2026 subject to RERA. Meghna One is a Grade A gold-certified green building.

guidance_outlook: Launches May-Dec 2026: Wagle Estate commercial (INR300 crore GDV), Khar residential (INR60 crore), Bandra West residential (INR240 crore), Juhu/Vile Parle West residential (INR50 crore); next launches adding over INR600 crore GDV by September 2026.
Upcoming portfolio GDV stated above INR2,100 crore; management aims to at least double it over the next two years, without giving a number.
Riviera OC expected within a month; Rivaan targeted for completion by December 2026 versus RERA deadline March 2027.
Management expects PAT to improve this year as project profits begin to be booked.
Approvals for seven to eight further projects with signed sign-ups expected in Q2 or Q3 2026 after BMC-level slowdown.
Acquisitions outside the redevelopment model to stay below 20% of GDV.
capex_capacity: Rivaan: 20-storey building, 17th of 20 slabs under construction; finishing on lower floors has started.
Kandivali project (over INR500 crore GDV): land registration done; height approval pending from MoD; company open to debt on this project, otherwise self-funded or pre-sales funded.
Construction area of current and upcoming projects to launch by December 2026 to exceed 1 million sq ft, with a similar increase expected over the next two years.
Biophilic facade design cited as cutting execution time by about 10-15%.
demand_pricing: Pre-sales typically 20-30% of inventory at each launch; Joshville about 70% pre-sold with about 15% inventory left.
Andheri under pressure from multiple launches; registrations on over 30% of Andheri pipeline expected in coming quarter.
Bandra/Santa Cruz/Khar project more than 70% sold.
Prabhadevi-Dadar sea-facing apartments selling at INR1.2-1.4 lakh per sq ft; company says its feasibility cost is much lower, enabling discounted entry pricing.
Price volatility in steel and cement: company seeks fixed-price contracts; management expects little impact on premium launches.
Realisation improvement attributed to premium project mix and maturing projects.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the about 12% rise in realisation: pricing or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift to more premium projects and maturing projects from prior-year launches, which lifted collections.

qa_highlights.question: Unsold inventory across ongoing projects and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Riviera has one unit left; Rivaan six unsold units with bookings pending registration; Pranam 30-35% conversion this quarter; Manju Villa three units; Joshville about 15% left.

qa_highlights.question: Which of the upcoming projects launch in FY27 and approval timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Wagle Estate launch 22 June 2026 pending RERA by end-June; Khar RERA delayed by pending approvals, bookings in Q2 2027; Bandra West launch Q2 2027 with bookings from Q3 2026; Juhu/Vile Parle slipping 15-20 days into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Kandivali approvals and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Land registration done; awaiting height approval from MoD. Self-funded so far; open to project-level debt, with pre-sales and accruals as main funding.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT and EBITDA margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Securities carry-over profits ended after the 2024 transition; project lifecycle delayed profit booking; higher delivery costs and acquisition costs compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative despite profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Company aims to stay nearly debt-free; cash went into acquisitions of future projects that management expects to lift GDV and profit.

qa_highlights.question: Pace of project addition and GDV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to at least double GDV over the next two to three years, citing INR2,100 crore pipeline; no specific number given on project additions.

risks_watch: Approval delays at BMC/MoD level: seven to eight projects waiting, Khar RERA pending, Juhu/Vile Parle slipping.
Negative operating cash flow and reliance on pre-sales for funding; Kandivali may need debt or JV partner.
Margin pressure: EBITDA margin fell from 29% to 22% in FY26; acquisition costs and project mix weigh on profitability.
Andheri supply pressure from multiple launches.
Steel and cement price volatility on contracts that are mostly fixed price.
Rivaan completion target of December 2026 versus RERA deadline of March 2027.
538668|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on pipeline and demand, but evasive on quantified targets (declined to give specific project-addition numbers or land holdings). Cautious on approval timelines, with several launch dates shifting.
key_quotes: So to be very honest, there is not a dip in demand. Demand actually is impacted of by supply more than anything else.
We are nearly debt-zero. We have always maintained that we want to remain debt-zero and that's why you will see a negative impact.
In the coming three years, and I will not give you a number, but you can expect us doubling the GDV overall.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, as project profits begin to be booked
rows.why: Management expects PAT to improve this year, and the company says realisation rose to INR52,571 per sq ft from INR46,822 on a premium mix, but EBITDA margin was 22% vs 29% and acquisition and delivery costs are weighing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 to Q4 FY27 (launches May-Dec 2026)
rows.why: Dated launch pipeline of Wagle Estate (INR300 crore GDV, 22 June 2026), Khar (INR60 crore), Bandra West (INR240 crore) and Juhu/VP West (INR50 crore) by Dec 2026, with over INR600 crore GDV by September 2026; construction area of current and upcoming projects to exceed 1 million sq ft, but RERA and approval slippage is already visible.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Collections rose 36.69% to INR24.92 crore and FY26 revenue rose 15.84% to INR46.2 crore, with Q4 revenue up 52.47% YoY to INR18.48 crore, and management targets project additions of three to five a year and GDV at least doubling over two to three years, though the doubling is unquantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Kandivali (over INR500 crore GDV) land registered but height approval from MoD pending and company open to project-level debt; no utilisation metric applies since this is a developer, and no firm capex plan beyond project launches was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides only to PAT improvement this year and an unquantified doubling of GDV over two years; no revenue or margin numbers were raised, and approvals are slipping.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Launch dates are already slipping (Juhu/VP West 15-20 days into Q2, Khar RERA delayed to Q2 FY27 bookings), seven to eight projects await BMC approvals, and EBITDA margin fell from 29% to 22% in FY26.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wagle Estate commercial (INR300 crore GDV, launch blocked 22 June 2026 subject to RERA) plus Khar, Bandra West and Juhu/VP West residential launches, adding over INR600 crore GDV by September 2026.

rows.label: Pre-sales and sell-through on launches
rows.why: Joshville about 70% pre-sold with 15% inventory left, Bandra/Santa Cruz/Khar projects more than 70% sold, Rivaan six unsold units with bookings pending registration, and registrations expected on over 30% of Andheri pipeline in the coming quarter.

rows.label: Negative operating cash flow and debt funding
rows.why: Operating cash flow was negative despite profit as cash went into acquisitions; management aims to stay nearly debt-free but is open to project-level debt for Kandivali (over INR500 crore GDV).

rows.label: Approvals and RERA timing (Wagle, Khar, Rivaan)
rows.why: Wagle Estate launch depends on RERA by end-June 2026, Khar bookings slipped to Q2 2027 on pending approvals, and Rivaan targets completion by December 2026 against a March 2027 RERA deadline, leaving a three-month buffer.

tone.note: Management was confident on the pipeline (INR2,100 crore+ GDV, premium realisation up to INR52,571 per sq ft) but cautious on approval timelines, with several launch dates shifting; analysts pushed on the PAT decline, EBITDA margin fall from 29% to 22%, and the lack of quantified GDV targets.

538685|2026-06.headline: Shemaroo Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6% to about INR 132 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR 2 crore from INR 56 crore.
538685|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was about INR 132 crore, down 6% YoY, with digital down about 17% to INR 56 crore and traditional up 5% to INR 76 crore. EBITDA loss narrowed sharply to about INR 2 crore versus INR 56 crore a year earlier, after about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend; excluding that, existing operations EBITDA was about INR 18 crore. Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. Management said this is the first quarter after the inventory charge-off exercise, now in a normal charge-off cycle, and guided to double-digit blended growth, EBITDA-positive for the year, and bottom-line positive next year.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of approx. INR 56 crore (call analyst cited 55.5 crore) in Q1 FY26
materially reduced YoY; no prior figure stated

segments.name: Digital media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 56 crore, down 17% YoY, as select B2B syndication deals were deferred on geopolitical uncertainty; consumer business grew on fresh content and ad monetisation. Management targets double-digit digital growth.

segments.name: Traditional media
segments.commentary: Revenue approx. INR 76 crore, up 5% YoY, helped by closure of B2B licensing deals that offset subdued ad environment. Management expects roughly flat traditional revenue for FY27, with near-term ad outlook subdued due to BARC ratings blackout.

segments.name: ShemarooMe (OTT, Gujarati)
segments.commentary: Acquired OHO Gujarati catalogue in April 2026 (over 22 Gujarati originals); released 10 new titles in the quarter. Company does not disclose subscriber, ARPU or revenue figures; management said it is about two years from OTT profitability.

segments.name: YouTube
segments.commentary: Approx. 9 billion views across channels in the quarter; Shemaroo Filmi Gaane passed 74.7 million subscribers and Shemaroo Entertainment 61.9 million. Management said views are seasonal but viewership share remains strong.

guidance_outlook: Blended revenue growth aim of healthy double digits over the next 2-3 years; digital targeted at double-digit growth, outpacing recent low-double-digit industry digital growth by a couple of percentage points.
Traditional media revenue expected flattish for FY27, not declining.
Aim for EBITDA-positive for full FY27 (conservative view); management expects bottom-line positive next year (FY28).
Debt reduction plan for FY27, but no quantified target given; quarterly fluctuations possible given geopolitical and BARC blackout impacts.
Aspiration of around 20% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years, not a committed target; management said it is not sure it will be achieved.
New-initiative spend to be cut by more than 50% in FY27 versus FY26; management said the company is on track.
capex_capacity: Content strategy shifted: new content creation scaled down in traditional, while new content acquisition is being scaled up in digital.
Traditional channel rationalisation possible; company now runs two FAST channels after earlier shrinking the number.
OTT (ShemarooMe) needs ongoing content and customer-acquisition spend (ATL, BTL and performance marketing); management said little upfront capex is needed.
Inventory of INR 348 crore at Q1 end; management said no remaining write-down risk and the company is now in a normal charge-off cycle.
demand_pricing: Digital decline attributed to deferred B2B syndication deals (geopolitical uncertainty) and lumpy B2B revenue; consumer digital grew on fresh content and better ad monetisation.
Traditional ad market subdued for a long period; BARC ratings blackout in recent month has hit traditional and syndication revenue.
Acquired content is priced competitively against other bidders, so new-content margins are lower than on legacy content already amortised or charged off.
YouTube Shorts monetisation has not moved meaningfully; company is focusing on connected-TV long-form content, and is only experimenting with micro-dramas.
FAST channel ecosystem globally has been shrinking for roughly 12-18 months; company is tracking it and scaling only if monetisation improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA excluding the new-initiative investment, and what revenue is needed for positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding about INR 20 crore of new-initiative spend, EBITDA would have been about INR 18 crore. Management said margin depends on both revenue growth and cost cuts, and on revenue mix, so it would not give a revenue threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the content library under-monetised, and what growth is expected over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no under-utilisation, citing 9 billion views in the quarter. Traditional monetisation is declining while digital is growing. The aim is healthy double-digit blended growth, outdoing digital industry growth by a couple of points.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 profitability and revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: A debt reduction plan exists for FY27 but no figure was given. EBITDA-positive for the year is the conservative aim, with bottom-line positive next year. Digital is seen at double-digit growth and traditional roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow digital faster, around 20%, given 9-10% CAGR over FY24-FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry underlying growth was low, and it would not burn cash to grow faster, since that would strain cash flow and the balance sheet. It cited its leadership in Gujarati entertainment.

qa_highlights.question: Which digital segments carry the highest margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin depends on content age, not platform. Legacy content can yield 80-90% margins, newly acquired content can be near zero or negative, and production work can earn 10-20%. YouTube is not inherently high-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin, and is 20% EBITDA the aim on a reported basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was not satisfied with current margins and aspires to upwards of 20% EBITDA in 2-3 years. It declined to say whether this is on a reported basis net of all investments, and said the structural shift in the media industry is a factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and inventory at quarter end, and is further write-down likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was INR 311 crore and inventory INR 348 crore at quarter end. Management said the company is in a normal charge-off cycle with no further rationalisation planned.

qa_highlights.question: How long until ShemarooMe reaches break-even, and will it disclose subscriber or revenue data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is about two years from OTT break-even. It does not disclose DAU, MAU, subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue, and said it has no current plan to start.

risks_watch: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY on deferred B2B syndication deals; lumpy B2B timing could keep quarterly digital revenue volatile.
Traditional ad market remains weak and BARC ratings blackout is hurting traditional and syndication revenue.
Debt of INR 311 crore against an EBITDA-positive-for-year aim; quarterly debt movements may vary.
Limited disclosure: no OTT subscriber, ARPU or platform revenue data, and no quantified debt target; analysts asked for more granularity.
YouTube Shorts and micro-drama monetisation still unproven; a possible YouTube monetisation policy update was not confirmed.
538685|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the operating trajectory and cost discipline, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give debt targets, OTT data, profitability timing, or a revenue threshold for breakeven. It acknowledged margins are below its own aspiration.
key_quotes: Every quarter, I think we should be seeing an improvement on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
Are we satisfied with it? Definitely not.
I think if I see a 2 -3 year perspective, I think definitely upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA improved from a loss of about INR 56 crore to about INR -2 crore, and ex the INR 20 crore new-initiative spend it was about INR 18 crore; new-initiative spend is to be cut by more than 50% in FY27, and management guides to EBITDA-positive for FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; content creation is being scaled down in traditional, and FAST channels were shrunk to two, so no new capacity is planned in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets digital double-digit growth and healthy double-digit blended growth over 2-3 years, though digital fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore in Q1 and traditional is guided flattish for FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says little upfront capex is needed for OTT and the company is in a normal charge-off cycle; capex was not discussed beyond content spend.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is conservative on EBITDA-positive (described as a conservative aim), and the Q1 revenue fell 6% YoY, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore on lumpy B2B syndication deals, the traditional ad market is weak with a BARC ratings blackout, and quarterly fluctuations were flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ten new ShemarooMe titles were released in Q1 and the OHO Gujarati catalogue (over 22 originals) was acquired in April 2026, so ongoing content launches are firmly under way, though no new brand or platform launch was named.

rows.label: New-initiative spend cut by over 50% in FY27
rows.why: New-initiative spend was about INR 20 crore in Q1 and management says it is on track to cut it by more than 50% versus FY26, which is the main driver of the EBITDA turn.

rows.label: Debt reduction plan for FY27
rows.why: Management confirmed a debt reduction plan for this year, but gave no amount, against total debt of INR 311 crore at quarter end.

rows.label: Inventory charge-off cycle normalised
rows.why: Management says no remaining write-down risk and a normal charge-off cycle now applies against INR 348 crore of inventory, which should stop the large write-downs that drove last year's losses.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost discipline, the EBITDA turn and content library strength, but evasive on debt targets, OTT subscriber data, profitability timing and a breakeven revenue threshold, and admitted margins are below its aspiration; analysts pressed on granularity and the path to profitab

538715|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
538715|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75
Record high; vs INR120-140 crores last year

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of FY26 revenue (about INR220 crores) came from PVC and UPVC, of which about INR60 crores was UPVC windows and the rest PVC profiles. EBITDA margin in this segment was higher than modular; PBT margin was about 16.6%.

segments.name: Modular furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.name: Plastic profile core segment
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (Bangalore/Jaipur)
segments.commentary: New vertical under Mr. Varghese with INR56 crores of orders and revenue starting in Q4 FY26. Management guides INR40-50 crores of FY27 revenue; it targets EBITDA margins of about 20%.

segments.name: WPC doors and WPC wall/ceiling panels
segments.commentary: WPC door line (about INR10 crores capex) has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27. Management expects about INR15 crores of FY27 revenue; WPC wall and ceiling profile lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of about 30% revenue CAGR while sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins; management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable.

538734|2026-06.headline: Ceinsys Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR158 crore (+1% YoY) but EBITDA rose 27% to INR39 crore, margin 24.4%; order book INR990 crore.
538734|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was INR158 crore, up about 1% YoY, while EBITDA grew 27% to INR39 crore and margin expanded 505 bps to 24.4%. PAT was INR31 crore, a marginal decline, with PAT margin at 19.6% (down about 59 bps). Order inflow was INR143 crore against about INR157 crore executed, lifting the order book to INR990 crore from INR880 crore. Management withheld forward guidance throughout, citing policy, and focused on receivables recovery (JJM dues), a proposed AI cloud JV, and undeployed funds from the earlier fundraise.

JV incorporation expected in about 1-1.5 months; due diligence (technical, market) to take 3-4 months; business model to be frozen after that, with commercial activity indicated for FY28.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions, aiming for vertical integration and margin-accretive deals; no deal announced. Acquisition multiples cited at 5-10x EBITDA.
Around INR230 crore raised earlier, of which INR130 crore received in March 2026 and INR100 crore in September 2024 (per management clarification).

Management said JJM-related bids are being deprioritised in favour of transport (ITMS/ATMS), energy and other geospatial opportunities where budgets are funded. Transport positive developments expected in 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline of the INR990 crore order book and the funnel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution spans 3 to 18 months, with O&M extending to 5 years; weighted average 12-18 months. Management said the funnel is strong and it will not give a numeric funnel figure or guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book roll-forward not match inflow minus revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said run-rate businesses (about INR50 crore of Q1 revenue) are not booked in the order book. Net order book increased about INR110 crore after INR157 crore of execution. Reconciliation to be sent via the IR agency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI cloud JV economics and will Ceinsys be an EPC player?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV is 50:50 with AI Fabric USA, targeting defence and government sovereign cloud. Management said it intends to be an AI solutions company, not EPC, with contractors used for construction.

qa_highlights.question: What are the receivables and JJM dues outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle at 164 days, flat. About INR100 crore of IoT/JJM dues expected by end of Q3 FY27, per the Maharashtra GR. Management said billing is being collected with no new build-up.

qa_highlights.answer: INR67 crore order already received. Two more in process, with one possibly in Q2. Management declined to commit on timing but said tender pipeline remains strong, and a large national program order could come in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why not a share buyback given idle funds and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said buybacks are funded from surplus operating cash, and the raised funds are for growth. Management said it would not invest only to deploy capital; acquisitions must preserve margins.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the large unbilled revenue (about INR320 crore at 31 March, per the analyst) is mainly JJM; it is expected to be billed and reduce over the next 2 quarters as government funds come in.

538836|2026-03.headline: Monte Carlo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36% to about INR280 crores and EBITDA margin hit 9.2%; FY26 revenue up 16% to INR1,276 crores, with FY27 guidance deferred to Q2.
538836|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR280 crores (up 36% YoY), EBITDA of INR26 crores (9.2% margin) and PAT of INR5 crores versus a loss of INR10 crores a year earlier. For FY26, revenue rose 16% to INR1,276 crores, EBITDA was about INR227 crores (17.81% margin ex other income) and PAT was INR112 crores (up 38%, 8.79% margin). Management said FY26 hit its guidance of 16% revenue growth, and attributed the Q4 turnaround to lower discounts, summer-season sales and provisioning taken in Q3. Management declined to give FY27 numeric guidance until the Q2 call, but reiterated that double-digit growth is on the cards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 revenue growth came from volume, and what drove it?

qa_highlights.question: Did the company see any consumer spending slowdown from inflation?

qa_highlights.question: Is the KUSUM subsidy available and included in IRR?

538979|2026-06.headline: Greenlam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR797 crore, with EBITDA before forex up 48% to INR81 crore and net profit of INR21 crore versus a loss a year earlier.

539046|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 13.5% to INR896 crore and PAT grew 164% to INR40.69 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 6.84% on the Middle East cost shock.

Q4 FY26 revenue was INR228.74 crore (up 20.45% QoQ, 9% YoY), but EBITDA margin compressed to 6.84% (INR15.64 crore) as freight, energy and raw material costs spiked after the Middle East conflict. The alu-zinc line was commissioned in late December 2025 and is ramping up in phases. Management said new contracts since April 2026 pass through the full incremental cost, and that H1 FY27 margins should recover meaningfully.

539056|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR178 crores and EBITDA 24% to INR90 crores (50.7% margin), with footfalls up 22%.

Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

demand_pricing: Order book ~4.4 GW as of July 2026, visibility of 24-36 months; 200 MW repeat LOA from NLC India in July via tender.
MOU for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean in June 2026; firm orders for 500 MW so far, balance 1 GW to be firmed later.
Indian wind additions of 1.4 GW in Q1 FY27; total installed wind 57.4 GW; management expects 8-10 GW annual additions over next few years.
Blended realisation for INOX Green's ~4 GW consolidated wind portfolio of INR9-10 lakh per MW (excl. GST); acquired portfolios expected to be substantially higher.
Wind World India: ~4.5 GW O&M portfolio, FY26 revenue ~INR580 crores, ~5% contracted annual price escalation; clients include Tata, ReNew, Greenko, Apraava, Hindustan Zinc.
Management said there is no preferential pricing for INOX Clean versus third-party customers.

qa_highlights.question: What was MW execution in Q1 and what is the FY27 estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give MW numbers; it now guides on revenue and margin rather than machine volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth of 30% and 20% EBITDA margin be confirmed for next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance; management reaffirmed 75% full-year growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, with significant improvement expected in Q2 and H2 weighting.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue flat YoY and is the company no longer doing EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed flat revenue to the pivot to equipment supply causing disruption; it said Q1 is at par with prior-year Q1 and that EPC continues within IRSL with ~40% of third-party orders turnkey plus 1.5 GW INOX Clean MOU and NLC LOA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables are high versus peers; how are EPC receivables accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are recognised under Ind AS 115 on risk-transfer basis and remain elevated until commissioning; management said receivable days fell in Q1 (figures not disclosed) and should drop substantially over the next 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR600 crore Green EBITDA guidance annual or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual basis, expected from Q3-Q4 FY27 post consolidation of acquisitions; management would not guide on FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are INOX Clean terms arm's length versus other customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are arm's length, INOX Clean is treated as a customer, and there is no preferential pricing for it.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to meeting the 75% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO cited only force majeure events; said the equipment-supply pivot carries no seen risk to deliverables.

risks_watch: Full-year FY27 guidance (75% revenue growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin) is H2-weighted with 70-75% of business in H2; H1 tracking is roughly 5-10% short of the 25% share per management's own math, so Q2 delivery is the first test.
Recognition of the ~INR400 crore deferred revenue from Q4 FY26, partly in Q1 and the balance across FY27; management did not quantify how much was recognised in Q1.
Receivables remain elevated until commissioning under Ind AS 115; receivable days and working capital improvement over the next 3-4 quarters are unquantified.

Wind World India acquisition completion in Q2 FY27 and consolidation of the ~6.5 GW acquired O&M assets; INR600 crore INOX Green EBITDA is annualised from Q3 and excludes the acquisitions until consolidated.
Gap between INOX Green's ~50% O&M EBITDA margin guidance and reported margins; one-time and life-extension costs cited, with separate billing of value-added services expected from this year.

RESCO (IRSL) listing timing, expected in about 2-3 months pending regulatory approvals; 4X prototype installation in August 2026 and commercial launch about a month later; INOX Clean related-party order flow.
key_quotes: And we maintain that revenue guidance of 75% growth over the previous year and an EBITDA margin of 20% to 22% on a consol basis is what we maintain our guidance for the full year basis.
This is an annualized business. So on a quarterly basis, it will be pretty tough for us to say.
INR600 crores was an annual guidance, not the quarterly guidance. I can't achieve INR600 crores in a quarter.
So over the course of next 3, 4 quarters, you will see all these numbers falling out drastically and the balance sheet improving big time.

539118|2026-03.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.
539118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

financial_highlights.change: down ~190 bps YoY; up ~48 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Return on capital employed / return on equity (FY26)

financial_highlights.change: INR101 crore vehicles; INR165 crore land and buildings

segments.name: Tonnage / volume
segments.commentary: Tonnage decline was 13% in Q1 FY26 and about 7% for full FY26; Q4 returned to about 3% YoY growth. April 2026 YoY volume growth was about 8% per management.

segments.name: Customer mix (Q4 YoY)
segments.commentary: New customers contributed about 17% of quantity, lost customers reduced volume by about 14%, and existing customers grew about 1%.

segments.name: Commodity mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Textiles and cloth about 17-18%, agri (equipment, fertiliser, pesticides) about 10-11%, others (industrial, pharma, books, auto) about 5-6% each. Management says petrochemical-linked goods such as plastics are seeing lower demand.

segments.name: Booking mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: TO PAY and PAID spot bookings about 80%, ACCOUNT customers about 15-16%, FTL about 6-7%.

segments.name: Door-to-door
segments.commentary: Share rose to about 38-40% of commodities from about 33-34% earlier; realisation is about INR1-1.5 per kg higher for door delivery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 tonnage growth guided at 6-7% for the full year, with at least about 2% sequential growth each quarter.
New branches expected to add about 2-3% to FY27 tonnage; about 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings, fewer closures).
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 20%+ (near 21% in Q1 FY27 per management), with some basis-point impact from the withdrawal of bulk fuel purchase.
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore: about INR100-150 crore for vehicles and INR200+ crore for land and buildings.
Depreciation not expected to rise materially because most new investment is in land (non-depreciable).
Fuel price pass-through via selective route rate hikes, chargeable-weight change (1 cubic feet from 8 kg to 9 kg on certain routes) and fuel surcharge in contracts.
capex_capacity: Fleet: about 6,000 owned vehicles per management; vehicle count fell from about 6,100+ to about 5,900 YoY, with about 500 additions planned in FY26 (100+ done, about 400 more by December 2026) and no scrappage planned.
Network: about 1,293 branches and 50 trans-shipment hubs across 24 states and 4 UTs as of March 2026; about 110 branches opened in FY26 with about 55-60 closed, net about 40-50.
Vehicle life: normal replacement at up to 15 years; earlier only for outdated or accident-damaged vehicles.
About 77% of fleet debt-free and 14% fully depreciated.
Hubs in pipeline: 2-3 locations including Nagpur and Raipur.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume growth came from new customers and return of lost accounts after contract restructuring; management says lost customers are returning due to service levels.

Fuel: diesel prices rose about INR3 recently; management said it has passed through on selected routes but not across the network, and that a 2x increase in rates within a week means pricing will be reviewed over 1-2 months.
Fuel procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as direct refinery purchase fell from 41% to 36% of volume (bulk purchase withdrawn).
Competition: most of the industry is unorganised; VRL says it is at a premium to unorganised operators but comparable to organised players and express cargo on corporate accounts.
Demand headwind: petrochemical and crude-linked goods such as plastics are seeing weaker demand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and what efforts drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 6-7% full-year tonnage growth and about 2% sequential growth per quarter, driven by completed rate rationalisation, marketing, new branches and new customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume pressure is from weak petrochemical-linked demand, not fuel prices. Hikes were applied on selected routes, with fuel surcharges in contracts; April 2026 YoY volume grew about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of lower bulk fuel purchase?
qa_highlights.answer: Some basis points of margin impact; management said it is flexible to hold EBITDA around 20% and the bulk purchase facility has already been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lorry hire charges rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet fell from about 6,100 to 5,900 vehicles while tonnage grew, so outside hired vehicles were used to carry the extra volume, plus higher lorry hire rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new branch contribution and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches contributed about 1-1.5% of Q4 growth; FY27 branches expected to add 2-3%. Depreciation is not expected to rise much, as land is a large share of new investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business mix and competitive positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is about 80% spot (TO PAY/PAID), 15-16% account, 6-7% FTL; door-to-door about 38-40%. Rates are at a premium to unorganised players and comparable to organised players.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility and geopolitical risk; the pass-through lag could compress margins in the near term, per management's own caveat.
Weak demand in petrochemical-linked commodities (plastics etc.) could offset recovery.
Reliance on hired vehicles (lorry hire cost rose) while owned fleet shrinks.
Achievement of 6-7% FY27 volume growth depends on net new branches (about 100) ramping up.
Management did not disclose kilometre-based metrics; lead distance is about 270-280 km and capacity 15-18 tons.

Answers on fuel pricing and competition were direct, while the company declined to disclose the bus-business question (not in business) and kilometre data.
key_quotes: And ultimately, the cost, whatever additional costs will come, that needs to be pass it on to the customers.
So, on a full year basis, we are expecting around INR300 crores to INR350 crores capital expenditure.
But definitely, on a full quarter basis, we are planning to maintain similar EBITDA numbers.

rows.why: About 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings) adding 2-3% to tonnage, plus 2-3 hubs in pipeline including Nagpur and Raipur, while the owned fleet shrank from about 6,100 to 5,900 and about 400 more vehicles are due by December 2026.

rows.when: FY27 (at least 2% sequential growth each quarter)
rows.why: Management guides 6-7% FY27 tonnage growth, with April 2026 up about 8% YoY, Q4 at about 3%, and new customers contributing about 17% of quantity against about 14% lost volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore (INR200+ crore for land and buildings) and utilisation read is not disclosed, so a land and branch capex plan is guided but not new.

rows.label: Return of lost customer accounts
rows.why: Lost customers cut Q4 volume by about 14%, and management says they are returning on service levels, which supports the 6-7% FY27 tonnage guide.

rows.label: Fuel pass-through via rate hikes and surcharges
rows.why: Diesel rose about INR3; hikes applied on selected routes, pricing review over 1-2 months, and contracts carry a fuel surcharge, though the network-wide pass-through is not yet complete.

rows.label: Weak petrochemical-linked demand (plastics)
rows.why: Management says plastics and crude-linked goods are seeing lower demand, a headwind that could offset the recovery in volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on the volume recovery (April 2026 up about 8%) and fuel pass-through, but cautious on near-term margins given bulk fuel purchase withdrawal; analysts pushed on fuel pricing, competition and kilometre data, which management did not disclose.

539118|2026-06.headline: VRL Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 81 crore (9% margin) on freight realisation up 9% to Rs 8,546/tonne and volumes up 9%.
539118|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 18% YoY to Rs 885 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs 193 crore, with margin up 71 bps to 21.8%, despite a sharp fuel cost spike (procurement cost Rs 83 to Rs 94/litre). Management passed through the cost increase via rate hikes of roughly 5% in the quarter, and volumes grew about 9% YoY to 10.19 lakh tonnes. Net debt fell to Rs 391 crore from Rs 440 crore, and the board approved a Rs 280 crore buyback at Rs 320/share, subject to shareholder approval. Full-year guidance is raised to about 8% volume growth.

Vehicle capex of about Rs 100 crore for the rest of FY27.

About 85% of LTL business is on PAID and TO PAY terms; receivable days about 10-12.
Bulk fuel purchase stopped as bulk price was about Rs 15/litre above retail when crude spiked.

Agriculture is about 10-11% of volumes; lower monsoon may slightly weigh on coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken and will it sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 5% was taken in Q1 across fuel-driven hikes, and it is sustainable; if fuel falls, rates would be cut 2-3%. Freight realisation of Rs 8,546/tonne would hold absent fuel changes and may improve further, as mid-quarter hikes are not fully in the Q1 average.

qa_highlights.question: Is 9% volume growth the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year volume growth now expected at about 8%, up from 6-7% guidance, supported by branch expansion and recovery of lost customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and how does it fund the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual FCF of Rs 480-500 crore funds capex of Rs 220-240 crore and the buyback; debt will stay at about the current level (about 0.3x debt-to-equity).

qa_highlights.question: Why buyback rather than debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback replaces dividend, as about Rs 175 crore was paid as dividend last year; debt is already nominal at about 0.3x debt-equity.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DFC and rail on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is in talks with the Ministry of Railways on hub-to-hub rail use; collaboration is minimal today and management says it would not hurt the customer-facing business.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka minimum wage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rule not yet in force (challenged in court); impact expected to be small as salaries are already above minimum wage, with only statutory contribution changes.

risks_watch: Fuel price path (Gulf/crude volatility): fuel cost pass-through works both ways, with rate cuts of 2-3% if fuel falls.
Sustainability of ~9% volume growth after the recovery of lost low-margin customers; full-year guidance raised to 8%.
Buyback of Rs 280 crore at Rs 320/share is subject to shareholder approval; promoters are not participating.
Lower monsoon could weigh on agriculture (10-11% of volumes) in coming quarters.

Shift in lead distances from East/Northeast expansion: management says the NTKM impact is only 2-3%.

539141|2026-03.headline: UFO Moviez Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to ₹1,342 mn and FY26 net profit rose 161% to ₹249 mn, though Q4 EBITDA fell 13% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Is UFO losing pricing power as ad-sharing with theatres rose to about 59.5% from 33%?

qa_highlights.answer: The CFO did not give an FCF figure. Net cash rose from ₹48.3 cr to ₹59 cr despite about ₹15 cr tied in working capital including TDS. Debt is raised for theatre equipment via LC-to-loan conversions, and the company keeps both cash and debt by policy.

539141|2026-06.headline: UFO Moviez Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,118 mn (vs ₹1,090 mn YoY) and advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, helped by Dhurandhar spillover.

539150|2026-03.headline: PNC Infratech FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR 4,633 crore; management guides ~30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 with ~12% EBITDA margin.
539150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 1,458 crore with 12.02% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 100 crore, while FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore was below earlier expectations due to delayed appointed dates on four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth), FY28 about 25% higher, and EBITDA near 12% in FY27, citing bitumen and crude-driven cost pressure partly offset by new escalation mechanisms. The company has an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, and it is diversifying into solar, BESS, coal mining and water. Net surplus on a standalone basis was INR 327 crore, while consolidated net debt to equity was 0.76 times.

segments.commentary: About INR 300 crore received in FY26 from state payments; FY27 revenue target INR 750 crore. Andhra irrigation: INR 380 crore work done to 31 March, ~INR 700 crore remaining, FY27 target ~INR 200 crore.

segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,956 crore over five years; FY26 turnover ~INR 68 crore; FY27 target ~INR 400 crore and FY28 ~INR 600 crore. Capex of ~INR 350 crore, of which ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26.

segments.name: Solar and BESS
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,000 crore in development; physical execution to start Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC. Revenue target INR 600 crore in FY27 and INR 1,400 crore in FY28; equity requirement ~INR 400 crore, ~INR 120 crore in FY27.

MoRTH cost escalation mechanism from 1 April 2026 for EPC/HAM/PBMC projects with monthly price adjustment (earlier three months); management expects revised authority cost or extended compensation for new tenders.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 rise was from working capital utilisation and term loan interest on machine financing; management expects a reduction of INR 3-4 crore from the current quarter.

539254|2026-09.headline: AESL Q2 FY27: total income up over 50%, EBITDA up ~67%, PAT up 145% as Energy Solutions earned strong merchant margins; smart meter deployment lagged.

Smart meter installations were slower than expected in H1, which management attributed to consumer resistance and utility-specified installation scopes. Transmission commissioning in H1 was minimal, with ROW issues in Gujarat delaying Halvad and Navinal, and management still targets some FY27 commissioning.

539289|2026-03.headline: Aurum PropTech Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue rose 10.2% QoQ to INR 123.85 crores, with second straight profitable quarter and FY26 revenue up 50.8% to INR 381.09 crores.

Continuing-operations PBT was INR 1.85 crores in Q4 versus INR 2.93 crores in Q3, so profitability is still thin on a pre-tax basis. Distribution was the main growth engine, with PropTiger reporting its highest-ever quarterly gross commission of INR 42.8 crores. guidance_outlook: Management said it could not give forward-looking statements but expects growth of about 40% YoY to continue over the next three years, citing a 40% revenue CAGR since inception.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned, given PE/VC-backed peers may be divesting?

qa_highlights.question: What is the SM REIT timeline and focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on commercial pre-leased Grade A assets given SEBI rules; pipeline being built with channel partners; launch targeted within FY27 subject to due diligence.

qa_highlights.question: How are AI benefits measured versus operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Performance metrics (conversion, connection rates, time to go live) to be tracked over a few quarters, with revenue per employee as the net metric. Employee count excludes outsourced staff and interns.

qa_highlights.question: What are PAT margin prospects by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution consistently profitable with 22-25% margins; rental still takes time due to NestAway platform, tech and go-to-market spend. HelloWorld near adjusted EBITDA break-even.

539289|2026-06.headline: Aurum PropTech Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 70.9% YoY to INR 111.84 crore and PBT turned positive at INR 2.31 crore, with Housing.com acquisition announced.
539289|2026-06.overview: Aurum PropTech reported its third consecutive profitable quarter, with revenue from operations of INR 111.84 crore (up 70.9% YoY but down from INR 123.85 crore QoQ) and PBT of INR 2.31 crore (2.1% margin). Management said PBT margins expanded 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins 1,320 bps YoY. The quarter also featured the announced acquisition of Housing.com, which management says is loss-making and targeted to reach profitability in four to six quarters; the company guided to a burn of about INR 200 crore annualised at Housing. Management also said the INR 112 crore sale of a building closed during the quarter, contributing INR 52.38 crore of other income from discontinued operations.

qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to upsell more SKUs within the Housing cohort and extend into transactions; tax structure evaluation is ongoing, with positions to be given in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics and loss at Housing.com and what are the priority fixes?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: monetise intent via transactions, increase utilisation of under-used Housing SKUs, ancillary cross-selling, cut top-heavy corporate costs, streamline sales team and marketing spend (Meta, Google). Target four to six quarters to break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What is Housing.com's FY26 loss and burn, and how does it compare with 99acres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Housing's current burn is about INR 200 crore annualised; FY26 numbers still under audit and to be shared later. It argued listing-only models carry losses and the transaction layer is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: How will dilution and ecosystem cross-selling be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Deora said the REA stake (24.9% post-deal) brings strategic value; Housing adds the top of the funnel for cross-selling to PropTiger, KuberX and Analytica. No numerical cross-sell metric was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be profitable at company level within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees potential for company-level profitability as existing businesses are profitable, but will guide after the Housing deal closes.

qa_highlights.answer: Shrikant Jagtap said a PropTiger revenue category crystallised on target-slab achievement in Q4 FY26; slabs unlock mainly in the second half, so the drop is seasonal rather than one-time.

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.
539301|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR432 crores grew 147% YoY, with management attributing it to both Aqua City demand and broader core-market strength. Revenue rose to INR318 crores from INR102 crores and adjusted EBITDA to INR150 crores from INR25 crores, mainly from Orchards Phase 1 in Bengaluru receiving BU. Collections grew 76% to INR336 crores and net operating cash flow was INR81 crores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 35-40% bookings growth, INR4,000-5,000 crores BD and 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales, and India Ratings upgraded the company to AA- (stable).

segments.name: Ahmedabad (Aqua City, horizontal)

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Orchards Phase 1 BU received, driving the quarter's revenue and profit step-up; Bengaluru stock close to INR3,000 crores. Three launches planned this year, including Sarjapur, which has approvals.

segments.name: Mumbai / MMR
segments.commentary: Mumbai stock of INR4,000 crores-plus GDV; two Goregaon redevelopment-related and BD additions. Goregaon saleable carpet area about 6.7 lakh sq ft, 35-floor-plus, about 4 years to complete; 2 Mumbai launches planned this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% over FY26, implying about INR2,100-2,200 crores (per Q&A).
FY27 business development of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV; INR2,600 crores already added in Q1; management leaning to upper band.

Management did not give revenue guidance; expects strong YoY growth in FY27 revenue but timing depends on OC receipts, some lined up in Q4.
Medium-term 25-30% CAGR target over 4-5 years; comfort debt-to-equity at 1:1.

Pen Khopoli project in Mumbai awaiting approvals; company hopes to launch at least 2 of 3 Mumbai projects this year.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand is strong; Aqua City plus broader core-market strength drove bookings.

Price increases expected to moderate after 3-4 years of strong appreciation; company does not underwrite large price hikes.
Bengaluru price uplift giving better margins on some older projects.
Management sees Mumbai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad each delivering 22-25% EBITDA; no Tier 2 plans for now.
Management sees annual residential absorption of INR3-4 lakh crores across the three focus markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aqua City-driven booking strength project-specific or indicative of underlying demand in Gujarat and Bengaluru?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination of both; the market is strong and stable and responding well to most projects, and underlying demand remains quite strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unrecognised revenue conversion and normalised margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin was boosted by Orchards BU; the 25% portfolio average is the base case. Revenue recognition is OC-linked and lumpy, so no annual revenue guidance is given.

qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 OCF was about INR400 crores; FY27 target INR400-500 crores. Q1 OCF of INR81 crores reflects higher construction outflow, which management views as positive catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity at 0.29x; management comfortable up to 1:1 and expects gradual debt increase, funded by OCF and debt lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores from operating cash flow plus debt headroom; BD cash deployment guided at INR600-1,000 crores in the year (land outflow INR600-900 crores per earlier answer).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Not today; management is considering it after a few years, starting with for-sale assets to test development before holding assets.

Net debt to equity rising from prior level to 0.29x as BD accelerates; management's comfort threshold is 1:1.
Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.
Labour and construction cost inflation is gradual per management but may pressure margins.

539302|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 2,121 crore, while FY26 order inflow of ~INR 7,210 crore missed the INR 10,000 crore target by about 28%.
539302|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 2,121 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 237 crore (+2% YoY, margin 11.17%) and PAT of INR 153 crore (+18%). FY26 revenue was INR 6,107 crore (+16%), EBITDA INR 750 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT INR 412 crore (+18%). Order inflow missed guidance after cancellation of a INR 1,563 crore BESS order by the West Bengal electricity department, and the water division faced certification delays. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, order inflow of about INR 12,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12.5%.

segments.name: Power vs non-power mix
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 57% power and 43% non-power; FY26 was 64% power and 36% non-power. Backlog is about 70% power and 30% non-power.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 94% domestic and 6% international; FY26 was 95% domestic and 5% international. International work is mainly O&M and manpower supply (Middle East, Nigeria), with international revenue of INR 327 crore in FY26 versus INR 292 crore in FY25.

segments.name: MDO (mining, KBP and SAIL/Tasra)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 MDO revenue was INR 226 crore, including INR 117 crore in March. Management targets INR 500 crore in FY27 and INR 1,250 crore in FY28, with EBITDA margin of about 15% now rising toward 20% at peak rated capacity (FY29-30).

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M is the highest-margin business at about 15-16% EBITDA. Management cites O&M order growth of about 8% and about 4,100 MW of O&M orders in FY26, including a INR 279 crore Mumbai Monorail/metro O&M contract.

segments.name: EPC / civil
segments.commentary: Construction margins are below 8-10%. The BOP EPC order for the 800 MW Singareni project from BHEL is about INR 2,550 crore. Electrical transmission work has ended and was moved into civil.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.

rows.why: KBP mine already producing since Nov 2025 (FY26 offtake ~1.6 Mt vs target ~5 Mt by FY30) and Tasra washery (INR 400 cr capex) is under construction, with ~4 Mt targeted by FY29; ramp is conditional on client offtake and CCL washery readiness.

rows.why: No new products, brands or models were discussed; the only new business lines are MDO ramp-ups already in motion.

rows.label: Water division stall
rows.why: About INR 900 cr contract value stalled pending central/state fund release, INR 128 cr awaiting certification and INR 90 cr receivable; management has stopped new water bids, so this drag persists.

539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall short of the 8% margin management had earlier signalled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would have been Rs 75-80 crore without the deferred tax charge and leasehold-land provisions, which brought it to Rs 70 crore for FY26 (about 7%).

Unit 5 and 6 start-up timing is unresolved; the Kharif season is lost and Rabi FY27 is the next opportunity.
Demand and fertiliser affordability at current prices; management said subsidy support is not yet adequate and noted a 10% government cap.

key_quotes: So, sir, let the market be matured. Let the market be accepting these new prices, which are almost three times of the raw material prices of our earlier.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue has already been cut once (Rs 1,500 crore to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore), demand is weakening as prices rise, Q4 revenue was flat YoY on chemical volume up 36%, and Unit 5/6 timing is unresolved.

rows.why: Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 chemical plants are mechanically ready but no product launch timing or product names were given on the call.
