rows.label: NBS subsidy adequacy for fertilisers
rows.why: NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but management says it is still insufficient for current raw-material costs, and a 10% government cap is in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q1 FY27 PAT margin of 8-8.5% and on Unit 6 being 90-95% complete, but cautious on Units 5/6 start-up, FY27 pricing and the Rs 350 crore Unit 3 project, deferring numbers to the CFO and IR; analysts probed the unexplained Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap and capex funding.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 280.1 crore (CEO remarks) / Rs 281.1 crore (CFO remarks)
Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

key_quotes: I believe this year will be much better than the last two or three financial years for the company.
So, I believe Q2 will be even better than Q1.
No, sir, you don't expect 10%. I did not say 10%. I said that we will come to the level of 8.5 %- 9%. I hope so.
Honestly speaking, after these sulfur rates came, we put our acid plants on low load.
First, you need value, then volume.

It was cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up, saying it is taking a measured approach, and it declined to confirm the 10% PAT figure, reiterating 8.5-9%.

rows.why: Sulphur requires advance payment at about USD 1,100/t versus USD 250-300 earlier, chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1, and Rs 303 crore of the Rs 512 crore capex is still to be spent, so working-capital strain is likely to persist until acid plants restart.

rows.label: Value-over-volume pricing stance
rows.why: Dispatches were stopped in mid-March 2026 to wait for higher prices, fertiliser inventory is being held, and Q1 revenue rose 10% YoY on volumes down 13% (fertiliser) and 39% (chemicals), so realisations are carrying the top line.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 turnover (Rs 1,250 crore, stretching to Rs 1,350-1,400 crore) and pricing, and cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up and on volume recovery; analysts pushed on the Q4-to-Q1 order slippage, the falling acid-plant load, and guidance that moved between figures.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR790 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR8.90 per share (445% of face value); outgo about INR835 crore

financial_highlights.metric: CGD EBITDA per SCM (FY26, excluding amalgamation impact)

financial_highlights.value: Gas trading about INR400 crore; CGD about INR450 crore; E&P about INR14 crore; renewables about INR5 crore

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Total trading volume was 10.2 mmscmd in FY26, of which about 5.3 mmscmd was intersegment sales to CGD; net external volume was about 4.9 mmscmd, down about 19% from FY25. Management guided trading margins of 4-6% and said FY26 included a one-off of about INR200 crore linked to a Petronet LNG regasification liability, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

segments.name: City Gas Distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

segments.name: Exploration and production (E&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA was about INR29 crore, but the segment is loss-making after depreciation. Reserves are stated at 6.71 mmboe. FY27 E&P capex is about INR100 crore for planned drilling.

segments.name: Power (renewables / GSEG and GPPC gas-based plants)
segments.commentary: Plant load factors were about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. FY26 segment EBITDA was about INR46 crore (renewables, as stated), and the segment reported losses due to forex and impairment items of about INR15 crore and INR23 crore. The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

guidance_outlook: CGD margin guidance of about INR5-6 per SCM was given, with a target of about INR5.5-6.5 per SCM; management said trading margins will be maintained.
Morbi price is about INR75 per SCM (non-Morbi about INR68) per management; June was raised by about INR1.5. Management said Morbi demand can reach 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, about 10% above the current level.
FY27 capex guidance: about INR1,000 crore for CGD and about INR100 crore for E&P; no capex for trading.
Gas trading volume is expected to grow 25-30% by FY30-31 from the current 10-12 mmscmd, with prices seen as reasonable from FY28-29.
Tax: about INR1,900 crore of tax losses remain to be used, so no tax is expected on profits up to that amount; the balance is to be used within about 8 years.
GTL demerger share listing is expected to complete by end-July 2026; the listing approval for new Gujarat Energy shares (about 93 crore shares total) is expected within 7-10 days.
capex_capacity: CGD capex guidance is about INR1,000 crore; E&P capex about INR100 crore for drilling a few wells.
Gujarat Energy holds about 36.8-38% of GSPC LNG (investment about INR1,700 crore), following conversion of outstanding amounts into equity; it became a subsidiary.
GSPC Mundra LNG regasification terminal utilisation was about 17% in FY26; it is now at about 35-38% from May 2026.
Management is exploring a dedicated propane import jetty, JT and storage tanks near Morbi, with port authorities in Gujarat under discussion.
Long-term regasification capacity at Dahej is 2.25 MMTPA; long-term LNG totals about 2.96 MTPA (about 10.66 mmscmd).
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic units on gas rose from 83 (1.66 mmscmd) in March 2026 to 710 units (about 8 mmscmd) by late May 2026; contracts are signed monthly.

Non-Morbi industrial pricing is about INR68 per SCM and Morbi about INR75 per SCM; an analyst's spot-LNG math suggested Morbi margins may be negative at current spot LNG prices, which management did not accept.
Sourcing mix (per management): APM about 2 mmscmd, New Well Gas 0.4-0.5 mmscmd, long-term LNG about 3.5 mmscmd (majority Brent-linked), short-term about 3.5 mmscmd.
FY26 gas trading sales by user: CGD companies about 52-53%, fertilisers about 27%, others (refinery, power, industry) the rest.
Two new long-term LNG SPAs signed in FY26 (Qatar Energy and Uniper, up to 1.36 MTPA combined); Qatar 1 MTPA ramps up to 2030; 2 cargoes already lost in May-June 2026 due to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current sales are about 8 mmscmd, with customers indicating up to 8.8-8.9 mmscmd. Pricing is about INR75 per SCM in Morbi and about INR68 elsewhere, indexed to exchange rate and calorific value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PLF was about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. Management is evaluating reviving the plants through alignment with other businesses. GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

risks_watch: Propane supply tightness supports Morbi demand, but a normalisation could cut spot prices and volumes; management said it would still compete.
Spot LNG price and INR/USD moves could compress Morbi and CGD margins; an analyst's calculation showed a possible negative spread at spot LNG of about $17-18/MMBtu.

The INR1,334.61 crore trading EBIT includes one-offs, so the recurring run rate may be lower (about INR1,000-1,100 crore per management); also watch intersegment transfer pricing, which shifts profit between trading and CGD.
The power segment (about 1,000 MW) is loss-making with very low PLF; its revival plan and the 700 MW PPA economics are unresolved.

Cash and other financial assets are unclear: management cited about INR5,000 crore cash, while the balance sheet shows about INR1,300 crore cash plus about INR5,500 crore other financial assets, including GSFS-placed funds. The company will provide a breakup.
Watch Q1 FY27 results (early August 2026) for the first post-merger quarter and EBITDA by segment.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.
capex_capacity: CGD capex of about INR1,000 crores guided for FY27; INR127 crores invested in CGD infrastructure in Q1.
CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.
Gas sourcing for CGD: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term, and about 69% short-term or inter-segment.
demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.
Management said spot prices near $20/mmBtu make gas costlier than propane, so volume recovery is unlikely near term.
Gas trading sourcing: about 20% long-term (Brent-linked, of which about 20% Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic, about 67% spot.
Gas trading margin: fertilizer marketing margin is fixed at about INR20/scm; industrial margins are market-driven. Management said there will be no negative trading quarters.
Morbi volume rose from about 0.4 mmscmd in April 2026 to about 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the Morbi cluster up 181% vs Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Morbi run-rate is about 3 mmscmd of gas versus about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources. Gas is priced about INR78/scm against propane at about INR65/scm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD sourcing: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term and about 69% short-term or inter-segment. Gas trading: about 20% long-term (about 20% of which is Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic and about 67% spot. Long-term share is about 28%, or about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent, targeted at 4 million tonnes or more by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gas trading margin high in Q1, and can it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to timely sourcing and Brent-linked long-term contracts. It ruled out negative trading quarters and maintained FY27 gas trading profit guidance of about INR1,100 crores on total volume, with a 4-5% margin target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is about INR7,200 crores, with a concrete deployment plan by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification. It cited dividends of about INR835 crores under Government of Gujarat guidelines.

risks_watch: Morbi volume sustainability: run-rate about 3 mmscmd versus 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the 1.8-2 mmscmd floor on one-month contracts and propane supply recovering.

Gas trading margin durability: Q1 gas trading EBT of INR726 crores against FY27 guidance of about INR1,100 crores, with management stating it is conservative; Q2 visibility limited by Middle East volatility.
CGD EBITDA below guidance at INR5.18/scm against the INR5.5-6.5/scm range; management kept guidance but gave no segment-level explanation.
Third-party gas trading volumes down to about 3.3 mmscmd from about 5 mmscmd, with recovery expected only in FY28-29.
Power segment utilisation very low (about 6% PLF at GSEG and 1% at Pipavav); revival strategy to be shared in a few months.

Pending items: GSPL Transmission listing expected early September 2026, the INR900-odd crore tax refund needing at least a year, and the intercompany transfer-pricing markup between gas trading and CGD.
key_quotes: The Gas Trading segment delivered strong profitability with earnings before tax increasing to INR726 crores in this quarter as against INR237 crores in the previous year same quarter, reflecting a growth of 206%.
Our focus remains clear to maintain the right balance between volume growth and sustainable margins while continuing to serve our customers reliably and efficiently.
No, there will not be any negative numbers. I think we stick to our guidance last time we gave around INR1,100 crores of profit from the gas trading business.
We expect this towards early September.
539336|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Q1 delivery and the gas trading outlook, but cautious on forward numbers, repeatedly deferring firmer FY27 figures to Q2 because of Middle East volatility. Evasive on segment margin detail, pointing analysts to the investor presentation and declining to break out per-segment CGD margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CNG network at 844 stations with 6 added in Q1 and more than 75 new stations plus about 70 upgrades planned in FY27, backed by INR127 crores of CGD infrastructure spend in Q1 and about INR1,000 crores CGD capex guided for FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: CNG volume grew 13% to 3.76 mmscmd and PNG industrial reached 7.17 mmscmd, but Morbi is expected to settle near 3 mmscmd vs about 5.67 mmscmd averaged in Q1 and third-party gas volume fell from about 5 to 3.3 mmscmd, with recovery only in FY28-29.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management committed to a concrete deployment plan for about INR7,200 crores of cash by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification, and the propane import terminal near Morbi is at site-shortlisting with capex over about two years.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Gas trading profit guidance held at about INR1,100 crores (one answer said INR1,100-1,200 crores) and CGD EBITDA guidance of INR5.5-6.5/scm kept despite Q1 CGD at INR5.18/scm, with Q2 named as the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Morbi run-rate about 3 mmscmd vs about 8 mmscmd in May-June and propane recovering from non-Middle East sources, plus CGD EBITDA at INR5.18/scm below range, leave the Q1 gas trading EBT of INR726 crores at risk of normalising.

rows.label: Morbi volume normalisation from ~8 to ~3 mmscmd
rows.why: Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd in Q1 and peaked near 8 mmscmd in May-June, but current run-rate is about 3 mmscmd with 1.8-2 mmscmd floor on one-month contracts as propane supply recovers after July.

rows.label: Non-Morbi industrial volume to 3 mmscmd
rows.why: Non-Morbi volume is about 2.04 mmscmd and management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

rows.label: Power segment revival
rows.why: GSEG plant at about 6% PLF and Pipavav at about 1% in Q1, with management to share a revival strategy in a few months.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 delivery and reiterated FY27 gas trading and CGD guidance, but cautious on forward numbers and deferred firmer FY27 figures to Q2 due to Middle East volatility; analysts pushed on the CGD EBITDA shortfall and segment margin detail, which management declined to break ou

539359|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36.2% YoY to INR138.46 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.02% on raw material and gas cost spikes.
539359|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue for FY26 reached INR482.95 crore, up 35.32% YoY, with EBITDA of INR71.03 crore (14.71% margin) and PAT of INR23.20 crore. Q4 EBITDA margin dropped to 12.02% from the 16-17% range management cited earlier, which management attributed to raw material, gas, freight and outsourced labour cost increases in March 2026. Management expects margins to recover toward 15-16% if the war-related cost disruption does not worsen, and guided Q1 FY27 revenue at a similar run rate to Q4. Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Large castings (gearboxes, transmission cases, differential carriers)
segments.commentary: Management calls large castings the main driver of product mix improvement, citing fewer competitors (about 8-10 in India for tractor large castings) and higher value addition.

segments.name: LFC (lost foam casting) via Meeta Casting
segments.commentary: Contributes about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book; management targets 30% in three years. Margin is about 1-2% higher than conventional castings.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet material; product development and qualification ongoing with three to four products developed. Initial contributions expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue target of INR600 crore; management says 15% growth for the next two years gets there. Also cited 15% growth for the company against 6-8% expected from customers in FY27.
Margins expected to recover toward 15-16% (EBITDA) if no further war-related disruption; Q1 FY27 revenue expected similar to Q4 FY26.

FY27 capex of about INR25-30 crore, of which about INR35 crore is for the 7,800 MT foundry addition (the figures on the 7,800 MT project were given inconsistently in the call). FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT, with about INR60-70 crore capex.
Long-term target of crossing 1 lakh MT capacity by FY28.
Target minimum EBITDA of 18-20% for planned US finishing operations, versus 14-15% in India.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 72,000 MTPA across Dera Bassi, Hoshiarpur, Mohali and Tahliwal. Utilisation about 73-74% (around 52,000 MT); management says 80-85% is achievable in FY27 if market holds.
FY27: about 7,800 MT green sand foundry addition, to be commissioned in H1 FY27, plus matching machining capacity. Capacity to reach about 80,000 MT.
FY28: about 2,400 MT of LFC capacity; capacity to cross 1 lakh MT. Management said LFC capacity mix would be about 70/30 to 65/35 (conventional/LFC) after this addition.
Greenfield LFC economics: 3,000 MT capacity at about INR75 crore versus INR120-150 crore for conventional, roughly 50% lower capex.
Hoshiarpur land acquired via ARC auction was withdrawn after litigation; refund received. Company is looking for fresh land in about two to three months for capacity beyond 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: Customers expect 6-8% growth in FY27 with H2 facing a high base; company expects about 15% from new products and projects.
Company says it gained share with almost all customers: market grew 16-17% while the company grew 34%.
Top three customers (M&M, Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts named) contribute about 50-55% of revenue.
Order book described as overbooked; Vishal's estimate of INR500-600 crore was affirmed as easily achievable, but no official figure was stated.

Raw material cost up about 4-6% in March; management says raw material is passed through with about a one-quarter lag, while freight pass-through is being negotiated (monthly for some customers, quarterly for others).

Exports started to South Korea (one lot shipped, another going); Europe being explored. US subsidiary (Omnia Engineering Inc., Delaware) acquired for $50,000 with up to $100,000 planned; not yet operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is installed capacity and maximum utilisation, and why have EBITDA margins fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT; utilisation about 73-74%, with 80-85% achievable this year. Margin fell to 12% because raw material prices rose sharply in March, aggravated by gas issues; recovery expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-6%, and gas, outsourced labour, manpower and freight costs also rose in March. Management expects a reversion to 15-16% margins if war-related disruption does not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and funding for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR25-30 crore, with about INR35 crore for the 7,800 MT project per management. FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT needs about INR60-70 crore, funded by debt and equity; FY27 funded by debt only.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and leverage comfort?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose to about INR180 crore this year, with interest cost about INR22 crore. Management said net debt-to-equity will stay below 1 at all times; comfortable at about 0.65.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US entity's margin profile and plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The US entity is aimed at direct US customers; initial work would be manufacturing in India, with later possible acquisition or a US plant. Finishing-only US operations are expected to give 18-20% EBITDA margins versus 14-15% in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LFC share of revenue and order book, and what is the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: LFC is about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book. Margin is 1-2% higher than conventional castings. Customers added include KION India (domestic) and one in South Korea.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin recovery depends on stabilisation of gas, crude-linked chemicals and diesel/freight costs; freight pass-through is still under negotiation.
Debt rose to about INR180 crore in FY26, with interest about INR22 crore; FY28 capex funding mix depends on equity raise plans that were not specified.
The 7,800 MT addition's capex figure was stated inconsistently (INR35 crore vs an earlier INR60-70 crore for the project); clarity needed.
Customer concentration: top three customers are about 50-55% of revenue.
Legacy components (about 60% of mix per management) carry lower margins; the new-component mix shift will determine margin trajectory.
US entity and export ramp-up are early-stage, with no revenue or timeline disclosed.

key_quotes: Production volumes for Q4 financial year '26 stood at 14,193 metric tons, taking the full year F '26 volume to 52,620 metric tons, the highest in any single financial year in the company's history
So, I mean, I don't see a very, very major impact of these cost pressures for a long term', short-term impact will be there, but not on long-term basis.
We do 100% machined castings. We don't give raw castings.

rows.why: Margin recovery is explicitly conditional on no further war-related disruption, gas, crude-linked chemicals and freight costs are still unstable, and the 7,800 MT capex figure (INR35 crore) was given inconsistently with the INR60-70 crore figure.

rows.why: US subsidiary acquired for $50,000 with up to $100,000 planned and not yet operational; South Korea exports started with one lot shipped and another going, Europe being explored; no revenue or timeline disclosed, and targeted 18-20% EBITDA vs 14-15% in India.

rows.why: Debt rose to about INR180 crore with interest about INR22 crore; FY27 capex of INR25-30 crore is debt-funded while FY28 LFC capex of INR60-70 crore depends on debt and equity, with equity plans unspecified; management says net debt-to-equity stays below 1 (about 0.65 now).

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, 15% growth, share gains and the 1 lakh MT vision but hedged on margin recovery timing, freight pass-through and capex funding; analysts probed margins, capex figures and debt.

539400|2026-03.headline: Mallcom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR147 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 185 bps to 9.34% on raw material costs.
539400|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR147 crore (+7% YoY), with EBITDA down 11% YoY to INR14 crore and margin at 9.34%, and PAT of INR6 crore (4.29% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR540 crore (+11%), EBITDA INR61 crore (11.21% margin, down 130 bps), and PAT INR30 crore; FY25 PAT included a one-time INR25 crore land-sale gain, so the years are not directly comparable. Export OEM realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and tariff-driven concessions, while the domestic business grew about 20%. Both new units (Sanand, Gujarat and Chandipur, West Bengal) are now commissioned and ramping up.

segments.name: Domestic (branded)
segments.commentary: Management says the domestic business grew about 20% YoY in FY26 and is the growth engine; branded business has better pricing power. Last month of Q4 was softer on cautious sentiment and gas shortages for some industries.

segments.name: Exports (OEM / white label)
segments.commentary: Realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and concessions to hold share. South America, Australia, Russia and Africa were described as doing well; Europe and US weak; Middle East okay. LatAm sales are white label.

segments.name: New products (PU coated gloves, PVC gumboots, nitrile)
segments.commentary: In-house manufacturing started as import substitutes; management says pricing is competitive with imports and margins are similar to company level. India PU glove imports estimated at INR80-90 crore.

segments.name: Sanand, Gujarat (workwear/Protec unit)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started; running at about 50% utilisation, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted from existing capacity.

guidance_outlook: Management says 10-12% revenue growth is the bare minimum for FY27 and it is confident of achieving it, with upside if conditions improve.
Management wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins over time, but said there are many ifs and buts at this stage; an analyst's 14-15% normalised margin framing was not explicitly confirmed.
Expects FY27 revenue growth to come more from domestic than exports.
Capex: INR34 crore spent in FY26; budget INR10-15 crore for FY27 and similar annual levels thereafter, covering maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur.
Expects to apply for a capital subsidy for Sanand, estimated at about INR10 crore under the state policy.
Expects debt, mainly working capital, to decline further and most debt to be repaid over about 4 years; finance cost could approach near zero in 3 years (analyst framing, CFO said 'possible').
capex_capacity: Sanand, Gujarat (Protec unit) has commenced commercial production; utilisation about 50%, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted.
Chandipur, West Bengal industrial safety shoe unit is fully operational; capitalised in FY26 with INR7 crore of subsidy received against INR14 crore machinery cost.
In-house manufacturing of PU coated gloves and PVC gumboots started.
FY26 capex about INR34 crore; FY27 budget INR10-15 crore, with ongoing annual spend in a similar range.
demand_pricing: Export OEM realisations fell in FY26 due to near-full-year prohibitive US tariffs, weak EU demand and concessions to retain share; price pass-through lags, especially in long-lead OEM business.
Input costs rose across textiles, leather, PU/PC/NBR polymers, driven by petro-linked prices, FX depreciation, freight and energy costs.
Domestic: price list revised twice in the last quarter; competitors also raised prices, and some stopped taking orders or cancelled open orders.

US: volumes fell, but management says this reflects tariff conditions, not product, quality or price. India is outside the US TAA list, so an FTA is seen as key to regaining share; order cycles run 3 months to 2-2.5 years.
Competition: China seen as better placed on raw material sourcing and currency; unorganised players expected to be hurt by the cost environment, which management sees as favouring organised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall, and which export product prices decreased?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower realisations were mainly in export OEM markets, due to weak demand and concessions to keep customers. Domestic price increases lag input cost rises.

qa_highlights.question: How much could 10-12% growth and a 14-15% normalised margin be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% growth is the bare minimum and it is confident of it. It wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins, which it describes as the profile it would like to maintain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and finance cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: no term loan; working capital debt is about flat YoY at INR110-115 crore. Expects further reduction and most debt repaid over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key domestic demand drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code formalisation, BIS standards tightening, rising worker awareness, wider distribution, more marketing and fleet, and import substitution. Management says domestic growth is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about INR34 crore; FY27 budget is INR10-15 crore, including maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur. Sanand subsidy of about INR10 crore is expected to be applied for this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market for PU gloves and PVC gumboots?
qa_highlights.answer: India imports an estimated INR80-90 crore of PU gloves; PVC gumboot market size was not quantified. Export revenue is also targeted for both products.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from petro-linked raw materials, FX and freight, with lagged pass-through to both domestic and export customers.
US market access: India is outside the TAA list, so recovery depends on a trade deal; EU demand and FTA timing also uncertain.
Sanand utilisation (about 50%) and ramp-up of new products against the INR40 crore revenue target.
Domestic demand softness in the last month of Q4 and possible cost-conservation by customers.
Subsidy receipt for Sanand (about INR10 crore) and debt reduction pace.
Q4 PAT margin of 4.29% and EBITDA margin of 9.34% as the base for FY27 margin recovery.

539400|2026-06.headline: Mallcom Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore, while EBITDA margin rose 317 bps to 12.51% on pricing and raw material relief.
539400|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue was Rs 110 crore, down 25% QoQ, driven by weaker international sales and West Asia disruption. EBITDA held flat QoQ at Rs 14 crore, with margin up to 12.51%, and PAT rose 5% QoQ to Rs 7 crore (6.03% margin). Domestic revenue of Rs 64 crore grew 10% QoQ and was the highest-ever Q1 domestic number; international revenue was Rs 46 crore. Management said port congestion and weak Western demand cost the company a targeted double-digit export growth.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 64 crore, up 10% QoQ and the highest Q1 domestic revenue to date; brand recall and the SMILE reseller programme (over 1,000 resellers) cited as drivers.

segments.name: International / Export
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore, down sharply QoQ on weak Western demand and port congestion; management says exports are about 55% of the mix. Europe is down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore for last year.

segments.name: Sanand plant
segments.commentary: Three lines now operating (helmets, foam caps, nasal caps); FY26 revenue about Rs 5 crore (Q4 only); FY27 minimum target Rs 40 crore, described as on track.

guidance_outlook: Management will not revise the Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition for FY28, calling it a stretch but still a goal.
Top-line guidance of about 10-12% growth maintained; management hopes to reach the Rs 600 crore level for the year.
Export and domestic mix expected to approach 50:50 by year end, which management called realistic.
Aim to return to the regular margin profile, helped by price pass-through and Sanand efficiency.
Europe expected to grow YoY this year, with a target to recover the lost sales over the next three quarters; the India-EU FTA effect is seen mainly from next year.
Working capital borrowings expected flat through the year; term loans taken for Sanand capex and incentives.
capex_capacity: Sanand plant: three lines operating; helmet, foam cap and nasal cap production underway; management looking to add further capacity.
New EN812 certified bump cap mould launched and manufacturing started at Sanand.
Ongoing machinery capex to add capacity (no new building or land spend), per CFO.
Newer Gujarat investments aimed mainly at domestic and branded markets, with some export; large export contracts not expected quickly.
demand_pricing: Export demand weak in the West; management attributes part of the export shortfall to port congestion and containers stuck at sea.
Roughly 60-70% of export sales are planned and 30% spot/L1-priced (about 30% of export is commoditised).
Raw material prices remain elevated vs pre-West Asia levels for crude-linked products; some easing seen versus March-April.
Price pass-through: own-brand pricing adjusted from the start of the crisis; white-label contracts lag and will be recovered over the rest of the year.
No FX gain in the quarter; the company says costs are largely hedged.
New FR workwear (EN/US certified) launched for own brand and white label; value-added products cited at about 60-70% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Are raw material prices trending and how should margins move?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude-linked products remain at escalated levels versus pre-war; overall RM costs are higher than at start of calendar year, with some easing. Pass-through is gradual because of long-term fixed-price contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much export growth was lost and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both weak Western demand and port congestion. The company had targeted at least double-digit export growth, which it missed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin base now and what about under-recovery and FX?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a base and the aim is to grow from here. CFO said there is no under-recovery after the price increases taken at the start of the quarter, and no FX gain as costs are hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its Rs 1,000 crore target for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not revise the target now, calling it a stretch, and levers include capacity, distribution, new geographies, FTAs and larger contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Sanand revenue target and new lines?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: minimum FY27 target of Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1. FY26 was about Rs 5 crore. Three lines are operating; more capacity is being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Have any large LATAM or US export contracts been won?
qa_highlights.answer: Some long-term contracts exist for workwear and footwear. Large new contracts are not expected quickly; US demand is uncertain due to tariffs.

risks_watch: Export demand in Europe and LATAM remains weak; Europe was down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1.
White-label price pass-through lags, so margin recovery depends on contract renewals within the year.
US tariff uncertainty and importer hesitation; no large US contract yet.
Port congestion and container availability disrupting shipments and Middle East supply.
Revenue must rise to earn back the fixed-cost absorption lost in Q1 (lower turnover).
539400|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and domestic execution, but cautious and somewhat defensive on exports, US and the Rs 1,000 crore target. Management stressed that volatility and logistics, not strategy, drove the export shortfall.
key_quotes: Despite the challenging and volatile market environment during the quarter, we delivered a meaningful improvement in profitability supported by lower raw material cost, improved operational efficiency at our Sanand plant, and our continued ability to pass on cost increases to our customers.
So, there is no FOREX gain because in our case, mostly we are hedged.
So, whatever cost increase was there, we have been able to pass on this to the customer, and we took this exercise at the beginning of the quarter itself.

rows.why: No large US contract has been won yet, US demand is uncertain due to tariffs, and management does not expect large export contracts quickly.

539404|2026-03.headline: Satin Creditcare FY26 consolidated PAT rose 79% to INR330 crores; Q4 PAT up 125% QoQ, with FY27 standalone AUM growth guided at 15-20%.
539404|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated AUM of INR15,174 crores (up 19% YoY), revenue of INR3,161 crores (up 23%) and PPOP of INR928 crores (up 23%). Consolidated PAT was INR330 crores for FY26, and Q4 PAT rose 640% YoY and 125% QoQ, which management attributed to lower credit costs and growth, not one-offs. Standalone GNPA was 3.1% at March 2026 and credit cost fell to 3.8% for FY26 from 4.6% in FY25, with Q4 at 2.5% standalone and 2.2% consolidated. Management guided FY27 standalone AUM growth of 15-20% and credit cost of 3-3.5%, and raised its 2030 consolidated AUM target to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores.

financial_highlights.change: NIM 13.23% in FY26 vs 12.42% in FY25

financial_highlights.value: FY26 3.8% standalone; 3.55% consolidated; Q4 2.5% standalone, 2.2% consolidated (INR79 crores)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 standalone -77 bps vs 4.6% in FY25

segments.name: Standalone microfinance (JLG)
segments.commentary: Standalone AUM INR12,853 crores (+14% YoY) with disbursements of INR11,202 crores; UP is 23% of portfolio with PAR 90 of 3%, Assam PAR 90 0.7%, Punjab 1.5%. Stage 3 coverage 73% (from 67% in Dec 2025); on-book provisions INR273 crores (2.9%) vs RBI requirement INR172 crores.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,267 crores, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA about 3%, CRAR 53.8%; ICRA A- stable. Average yield about 15.5-16%.

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL, MSME subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,054 crores, up 92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; 121 branches in 14 states; disbursed INR255 crores across 34 green loans. Lending is secured by receivables, equipment and property, per management.

segments.name: Satin Technologies (STL)
segments.commentary: Enterprise tech (HRMS, LMS, core banking, cybersecurity, agentic AI); first two clients within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives (SGAL)
segments.commentary: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF, a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs; MOU with SBI for co-investment; progressing toward first close with soft commitments.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone AUM growth 15-20% YoY, implying about INR14,800-15,100 crores.
FY27 standalone credit cost target 3-3.5% vs 3.8% in FY26.
Consolidated AUM growth management estimate about 25-30% (average), so consolidated AUM roughly doubles toward the 2030 target.
2030 consolidated AUM target raised to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores; non-MFI share target 30% (17% today).

NIM expected stable at about 12-13% consolidated (management also cited 13.5-14% over a longer period); no explicit ROA guidance, but management said ROA should improve on FY26's 2.6%, and that a >3% ROA is 'positive' rather than guided.
Cost of funds expected stable to lower; management says it could fall further as repo rates decline.

Consolidated PAT is sensitive to forex and treasury gains: INR144 crores consolidated derecognition gain, of which INR92 crores is FX-related; management says this reverses over time.
Q4 PAT surge partly reflects lower credit cost; sustainability depends on the 3-3.5% FY27 credit cost target being met.
Yield regulation: incremental MFI yield about 25% and RBI commentary on interest rates; management says the pricing is justified but did not comment on future caps.
Subsidiary ramp-up (SGAL first close, STL client wins) is still early; the consolidated 25-30% growth and 30% non-MFI mix by 2030 depend on it.
Standalone net worth (INR3,129 crores) exceeds consolidated (INR2,868 crores) due to an old revaluation gain, which has limited analytical value.
539404|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on asset quality, profitability and diversification, with strong claims on Q4 performance. Management was evasive on specifics: declined to give ROA guidance, the April collection-efficiency number and the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT, and gave a vague answer on the RBI yield question.
key_quotes: Consolidated PAT grew 640% year -on-year and 125% quarter -on-quarter.
There's no one-off.
We are not growing blindly. We are growing into our infrastructure with the discipline that has defined Satin.
So there is no question where I think it could be singled out as in terms of tax and it's an interest rate play which is going to be there.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said SFL serves graduated MFI customers and green-finance/micro-enterprise borrowers, underwrites on cash flows and internal scores with data analytics, and lends on secured terms (receivables, equipment, property). It did not give a percentage of the book secured by property; LTV is about 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for April X-bucket collection efficiency and whether geopolitical issues are causing stress.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April is holding at a similar level to Q4 (99.9%) but did not give a figure, and said there is no stress from the geopolitical situation in any state. Q4 overall collection efficiency was a little over 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether there was any one-off in Q4 PAT, including forex.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off; Aditi Singh attributed the Q4 PAT rise to reduced credit cost and the growth strategy. Management did not separately quantify the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 ROA guidance and whether ROA above 3% is achievable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give explicit ROA guidance, saying it is a function of AUM growth and credit cost; it said it expects ROA to be better than FY26's 2.6% and that the direction is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the consolidated AUM path to the 2030 target and the growth pace.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15-20% guidance applies to standalone MFI only; consolidated growth is expected to average about 25-30%, which supports the revised INR32,000 crore 2030 AUM target (from INR25,000 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR144 crore net gain on derecognition of financial instruments and whether treasury income is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated INR144 crore line includes a INR92 crore FX effect offset by a corresponding finance-cost item, while derecognition gains are DA income and fair-value gains are treasury income on mutual funds and forex contracts. Management said treasury income is incidental to liquidity, and that NIM is broadly stable at 13.5-14% over a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the RBI yield-cap risk and whether the MFI yield of about 25% is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator's interest-rate focus should be read in the context of financial inclusion, doorstep delivery, elevated credit cost and cost of funds, and risk-based pricing. It did not say how it sees future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut.

SGAL: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF; progressing toward first close with strong soft commitments; MOU with SBI for co-investment.

Management said standalone AUM growth of 15-20% in FY27 rests on branch infrastructure and ALM, and said it is growing into existing infrastructure rather than growing blindly.

rows.label: RBI yield-cap risk on MFI pricing
rows.why: Incremental MFI yield is about 25%, management gave no view on future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut, so a regulatory cut to yields is a live risk.

rows.label: Subsidiary ramp-up: SFL and SHFL growth
rows.why: SFL AUM INR1,054 crores (+92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%) and SHFL AUM INR1,267 crores (3-year CAGR 36%) keep the non-MFI mix rising toward the 30% by 2030 target from 17%.

539404|2026-06.headline: Satin Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 182% YoY to INR120 crore after absorbing a INR36 crore management overlay; reported ROA 3.55%.
539404|2026-06.overview: Satin reported its 20th consecutive profitable quarter and its strongest Q1 in eight years, with consolidated AUM of INR15,935 crore (up 27% YoY, 5% QoQ) and record Q1 disbursements. Standalone NIM rose to 14.36% from 13.16% and cost-to-income improved to 44.49%. Management chose to absorb a INR36 crore management overlay, which lowered reported ROA to 3.55% (4.34% adjusted) and ROE to 15.10% (18.46% adjusted). Guidance for FY27 was kept at 20-25% consolidated AUM growth, 3-3.5% credit cost and 3.5-4% reported ROA, with a review at the half year.

financial_highlights.change: from 13.16% YoY; DA income INR94 crore in Q1 vs ~INR140 crore in Q4

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,360 crore, up 134% YoY and 29% QoQ across 121 branches in 14 states; CRAR 27.1%.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (SHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,263 crore, up 31% YoY; CRAR 59.8% across 57 branches in 22 states.

segments.name: Green finance book
segments.commentary: Reached INR624 crore; INR294 crore disbursed across 50 loans in Q1; ~45% of sustainable and emerging businesses portfolio in clean mobility and renewables.

segments.name: Satin Technologies / QTrino Labs
segments.commentary: First paying HRMS customers in Q1; QTrino Labs reached first customer revenue milestone. Core banking platform in customer UAT, go-live targeted Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives
segments.commentary: Progressing toward first close of Category 2 AIF, with first deployment expected in the coming quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated AUM growth of 20-25% in FY27, implying INR18,200-18,900 crore by March 2027.
Standalone reported credit cost of 3-3.5% for FY27, inclusive of any buffer built.
Standalone reported ROA of 3.5-4% for FY27; management expects QoQ ROA improvement from the 3.3% consolidated level.
NIM expected to stay in a 14.35-14.50% steady-state range.
Guidance to be reviewed at the half year depending on monsoon; long-term target INR32,000 crore consolidated AUM by 2030 with 30% from non-MFI.
Non-MFI share of consolidated AUM at 19% vs 14% a year ago; target 30% by 2030.
capex_capacity: Added 41 standalone branches in Q1; total 2,041 branches, 34 lakh clients, 3.9 lakh centres, 18,518 employees.
Commenced operations in Kerala in June 2026, adding to Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
392 branches added in FY26 are seasoning; operating expense ratio improved to 6.33% from 6.98% in Q4.
AUM per loan officer up 29% YoY.
Breakeven rule of thumb for a new branch: about 1,000 customers, typically reached in about 9 months.
INR100 crore promoter infusion approved by shareholders at about a 17% premium to the minimum issue price, to fund subsidiary growth.
demand_pricing: Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter; management called Q1 disbursements the highest first-quarter disbursements in company history.

Assam floods hit 3 districts (Jorhat, Sivasagar, Charaideo): about 44,000 borrowers and INR149.83 crore outstanding affected, of which INR96.95 crore is covered by nat-cat insurance. Management says Assam ex-those districts is 100% on target.
Bank share of outstanding MFI loans fell to 26.4% from 32.6% a year ago; NBFC-MFI share rose to 43.7% from 38.9%.
Marginal cost of borrowing down 37 bps YoY to 10.52%; 77 active lenders; top 10 lenders are 52% of borrowing; INR2,000 crore direct assignment sanction from a public sector bank.
Undrawn sanctions of INR2,600 crore; INR3,000 crore raised in the quarter including INR285 crore subordinated debt (sub-debt total INR497 crore).

qa_highlights.question: How large should the management overlay buffer be built annually or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not committing to a number; the buffer depends on macro and field conditions and may not be needed. On-book provision is INR250 crore against an RBI requirement of INR152 crore.

qa_highlights.question: DA income trajectory and sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: DA is kept at 20-22% of AUM; Q1 DA was INR94 crore (Q4 was heavier at about INR140 crore). Q2 and Q3 should be in a similar range; Q4 is seasonally heavier.

qa_highlights.question: Gross slippages and write-offs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were INR49 crore (vs INR90 crore in Q4). Write-offs were INR127 crore, elevated because GNPA fell by about 90 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Stress from monsoon or Assam?
qa_highlights.answer: Assam is covered largely by nat-cat insurance; only about 5% of the Assam portfolio (INR149 crore) is affected, of which 3.5-4% is insured, leaving about 1% exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated AUM guidance lower than last quarter's 25-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says guidance is deliberately conservative; it expects to achieve 20-25% and stable-state growth of 20-25% in FY28 is not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is credit cost up while asset quality improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages halved to INR49 crore and GNPA fell 90 bps, but the overlay rose from a little over INR20 crore to INR36 crore, lifting reported credit cost.

risks_watch: Monsoon impact on rural cash flows over the next 2-3 months; Assam collections in the three flood-hit districts.
Negative carry from surplus liquidity: quarter-end drag about 0.15-0.20%, lower over the full quarter per management.
Forex: INR3 crore net negative impact in Q1 from hedged ECB (INR1,573 crore outstanding) accounting mismatch between servicing income and finance cost.
Subsidiary returns remain dilutive during scale-up; consolidated ROA is in an investment phase.
Credit cost guidance of 3-3.5% reported; further overlay additions would depress reported ROA.
key_quotes: We chose not to because we have just come through a cycle in which returns across the sector swung violently and we don't want to be among those who report their best numbers at the top and having nothing left when the turn comes.
So we are not committing a number to it. It will all depend on how the macroeconomics as well as the field level things pan out to be.

But what our idea is, we look at the complete ecosystem and the way how the field operations pan out to be, and that is the reason why we came out with this number and try and look at that and build that kind of a software.
But it's not a guidance. But having said that, we will probably be in the same bracket in the stable zone even in FY28.
Now 15.85% as compared to 14.50% is a slight aberration because the last quarter, as I always said, is probably the most heaviest quarter.
539404|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and franchise durability, but deliberately cautious on returns: management chose to absorb a INR36 crore overlay and repeatedly framed guidance as conservative. Evasive on the size and cadence of future buffers, stating no number is committed, and on the FY28 growth outlook, which it called a stable-state view rather than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain: Is the 150-160 bps credit cost guidance right, and what is being seen on El Nino, oil and macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said 0-30 DPD data show no problem yet and that the bank is comfortable for the next 1-2 quarters; El Nino and drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka will be watched in Q3-Q4. He confirmed that credit cost of 1.5-1.6% is reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain: Why did mortgage GNPA rise and credit card SMA inch up?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage GNPA went from 1.27% to 1.54%, attributed to normal book ageing with the book not being pushed given low yield and near-nil YoY growth. Credit card GNPA fell from 1.99% to 1.49%, while card SMA rose from 1.35% to 1.49%, described as normal quarter-to-quarter variation.

qa_highlights.question: Param Subramanian (Investec): Is 55% incremental cost-to-income a multi-year commitment, and what is the steady-state liability drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said 55% is firmly expected for FY27 and H2, and depends on the roughly 500 bps gap between income and opex growth held for three quarters. On liabilities, he put the current drag at about 0.7% of average retail liabilities (about INR1,500 crore net of tax) and expects it to fall toward zero over about 3 years, with asset ROA of 1.3% seen rising.

qa_highlights.question: Param Subramanian: Confirm the NIM waterfall, Q3 and Q4 path, and asset-mix effect.
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhanshu said a 25 bps repo hike has already happened and one more is assumed in the next quarter; about 32% of the book is repo-linked. Q3 NIM should be range-bound, with recovery to about 5.8% in Q4 from the 7 bps liquidity drag reversing, 8 bps day-count benefit, and repo hikes. Vaidyanathan said the 2-quarter view already factors in asset mix.

qa_highlights.question: Piran Engineer (CITIC): Does September NIM lag the Q2 average, and is the 5.8% guidance excluding a capital raise? Also, why has CASA growth slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhanshu said September NIM was slightly lower due to high LCR, but Q3 should be range-bound before picking up in Q4. The 5.8% guidance excludes any capital raise, which would be additive. On CASA, average CASA growth is about 23% YoY; Vaidyanathan said the bank intends to hold CASA in the high 40s.

qa_highlights.question: Piran Engineer: What is the corporate book's composition, rating profile and ROA case versus retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said A-and-above rated make up 76% of the corporate book, BBB 20% and BB-and-below 4%. Net book is about INR70,000 crore against about INR1 lakh crore including non-funded. Only one ATM company loss of about INR100 crore in 7 years. Corporate cost-to-income is about 32-33% and yield about 9.2% (corrected from 9.5%), implying ROA of 1.6-1.7% at nil credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: Abhishek Murarka (HSBC): Are the insurance commission impacts fully offset by FCNR savings and rate hikes, and what is the quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaidyanathan said management assumes the 25 bps hikes already done plus 25 bps more in FY27 and 25 bps in April 2027, and expects FCNR benefit and product changes to offset the insurance impact. He declined to give a quantum. Sudhanshu put FCNR-related fee income at about INR30 crore and opex at about INR60 crore in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Jai Prakash Mundhra (ICICI Securities): Any further ECB pipeline, LDR outlook, fixed/repo split, and ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further foreign borrowing pipeline. Deposit flows will be slightly above loan growth, so LDR should stay flat or improve. About 60-62% of the book is fixed (including FCNR), 31-32% repo-linked and the balance MCLR. Sudhanshu said the revised operational-risk RWA rules effective April 1, 2027 should broadly offset ECL capital impact on CET1, with more clarity in about a quarter.

risks_watch: El Nino and drought in Maharashtra, Karnataka and other states: management says no impact yet but Q3-Q4 is the watch window for rural and retail stress; credit cost guided at 1.5-1.6%.

NIM path: Q3 range-bound, recovery to about 5.8% in Q4 depends on repo hikes (two assumed, one in December and one in April 2027), excess liquidity deployment and the day-count benefit; FCNR repricing and funding cost rise could offset it.
IRDAI commission consultation could reduce fee income; offsets (repo hikes, FCNR benefit, product mix) are not quantified by management, and the regulation is expected to take effect next year.
Mortgage GNPA rose to 1.54% from 1.27% YoY and card SMA rose to 1.49% from 1.35%; watch whether these trends continue.
CASA ratio fell to 47.6% (average 48.4%) with FCNR in the denominator; management says it aims to keep it in the high 40s, and average CASA growth slowed to about 23% YoY.
Corporate and wholesale book growing above 30% YoY, now about 20% of loans; a single ATM-company loss of about INR100 crore is the only delinquency cited in 7 years.
Capital: CET1 13.01%; a capital raise is under consideration but excluded from the 5.8% NIM outlook; ECL transition and the April 2027 operational-risk RWA rules are still being fine-tuned.
key_quotes: So I can safely say that the trajectory is fairly established by now.
So we feel that we can reasonably give or take, stay in this zone for the next few quarters as well.
As of now, our data numbers don't seem to suggest that there is a problem coming.
We're actually seeing credit card costs coming down actually.

539448|2026-03.headline: IndiGo posted a Q4 FY26 net loss of 25.4 billion rupees, driven by 48.2 billion rupees of FX losses; FY26 underlying profit ex-FX and exceptionals was 75 billion rupees.
539448|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by the December operational disruption tail, a March demand break from Middle East escalation, and a sharp rupee depreciation of about 5% in the quarter. Total income for the quarter was about 238 billion rupees (up about 3%), and EBITDAR ex-FX was 64.4 billion rupees at a 28.7% margin versus 31.0% a year earlier. Q4 capacity growth slowed to 3% (about 10% in Jan-Feb) and PRASK fell 4% to 4.46 rupees. Management guided to a mid-teens PRASK increase for Q1 FY27 on fuel charges and a low base, but flagged higher costs and a seasonally softer period from mid-June, with capacity recalibration planned.

qa_highlights.question: Are fares fully passing through cost pressures, domestic versus international, and what is the international utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic fuel pass-through is largely recovered; international fuel is at market prices and only partly passed through via a fuel charge. International load factors were low in March and April, improving in May; no firm standalone international load-factor figure given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the mid-teens PRASK growth is base effect versus demand strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY26 May was extremely weak due to Pahalgam-related disruption, so the base is low; May demand is positive, and PRASK reflects both yield and load factor.

qa_highlights.question: Will fleet deliveries change?
qa_highlights.answer: No change to deliveries; near-term flexing via returning damp leases (narrowbodies) and reducing older CEO-generation aircraft given fuel burn.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASK ex-fuel ex-FX outlook and rupee sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to mid- to high-single digit increase. FX sensitivity is still about 900 million rupees per 1 rupee move; net dollar exposure about 10 billion rupees, with about 1.3 billion rupees hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging policy change given rupee volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge ceiling raised from $1 billion to $3 billion: $1 billion for 12-month cash flows and $2 billion over 2 to 5 years; hedged position currently $1.3 billion. Fuel hedging is at an early internal-deliberation stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Reversal of accruals for leadership payouts; year-on-year cost growth in line with normalised inflation and salary increases.

539448|2026-06.headline: IndiGo swung to a net loss of INR 2.4 billion in Q1 FY27 as fuel CASK rose ~80% YoY, despite yield growth of 21.3%.
539448|2026-06.overview: IndiGo reported total income of INR 256 billion (up ~19% YoY), with EBITDAR of INR 38.3 billion at a 15.6% margin versus 28% a year earlier. Net loss was INR 2.4 billion against a profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency the loss was about INR 56 million. Yield rose 21.3% and load factor fell 1.3 points to about 83%, but fuel cost rose sharply on Middle East-linked jet fuel prices and the rupee's depreciation of more than 11%. For Q2 FY27 management guided flattish capacity and PRASK growth above 25%, while holding the single-digit FY27 ASK guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Load factor fell only 1.3 points in Q1; Q2 loads expected flattish to slightly down as capacity is cut, with pricing discipline holding.

qa_highlights.question: Has fuel consumption per ASK changed, and what was the effective fuel rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption per ASK unchanged; only the rate moved. Management described the April-8 June domestic cap (25% on a March reference), VAT/excise, and market-priced international and private supply, with an average around INR 140-150/litre.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fuel CASK increase of ~63% QoQ reconcile with the OMC price-cap releases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to March being an elevated base, the capped domestic formula plus taxes, market-priced international fuel, and private suppliers pricing at market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 capacity guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: No change: FY27 ASK growth still single digits. Mid-teens growth is still held for FY28-FY30 (described as early double digits to mid-teens).

qa_highlights.question: Any risk of having to compensate OMCs for April-May fuel support?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the April-8 June bills were settled on the agreed formula, and it expects no extra burden because fares were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FX loss and supplementary rental trends?
qa_highlights.answer: FX mark-to-market loss was about INR 80 million; the rupee moved only about 10 paise over the quarter, on a USD exposure of about USD 8-9 billion. Supplementary rentals rose on currency and escalation, with a Q4 release base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields hold after fuel normalises?
