segments.name: India Fragrance and Flavours (mature)
segments.commentary: Management put the mature India fragrance and flavours base at about Rs 1,300-1,400 crore, with flavours volumes growing rapidly and margins improving on operating leverage. India volumes dipped slightly in March due to Middle East shipment delays, since restored.

segments.name: Aroma Global Ingredients / Middle East / Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Management called Middle East and Southeast Asia phase 2 growth markets. Q4 rest-of-world sales grew about 34% YoY per analyst question; Southeast Asia factory built last year with break-even reported.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Growth was muted over recent quarters because of capacity constraints. The Almere, Netherlands plant is now fully operational, with about Rs 10 crore of annual sales transferred on day one; management targets a return to double-digit growth.

segments.name: US and UK development centres
segments.commentary: US centre started last year and Manchester UK centre started this year. Management said US business of about 1 million (about 200,000 already in hand) is contracted; these are seen as 3-4 year ramps, with Rs 80-85 crore annual opex across three new centres.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain adjusted EBITDA at about 13% to 13.5% through H1 FY27, with Q1 more visible and Q2 subject to monitoring; it wants to keep EBITDA above 12-13%.
Gross margin expected at about 42% and thereabouts in H1 FY27, with absolute profitability to be protected via pricing pass-through.
Management said it is confident of achieving Rs 300 crore-plus EBITDA in FY27 and at least FY25 levels, with more visibility on H1.
FY27 capex is expected at about Rs 140 crore, mostly front-loaded in the first two quarters.
Borrowings expected around Rs 800 crore in FY27; gross debt may rise in the next 3-6 months before falling, with a target to reduce debt by 10% every year over the long term.
Management declined to give full-year FY27 guidance, citing raw-material and inflation uncertainty beyond H1.
capex_capacity: Almere greenfield factory in Netherlands is fully operational, debottlenecking European growth that was near full utilisation.
Vanavate facility in Maharashtra expected to go on stream in coming months, likely around end of current quarter, with a six-month transition from the Mulund factory; Mulund to close next year.
Vashivali facility rebuild restarted after a fire; it may be available around Q3 FY27 but may not be needed immediately, with full operation next year.
Creative development centres in Germany (labs functional for a couple of months), Manchester UK, and US are the new opex-heavy initiatives, with break-even in about 3 years.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inventory prices are up about 12-13%+; power and fuel costs are also rising. About 40% of raw materials are directly crude-linked and about 30% indirectly linked.
Management said price increases have been secured from many clients, including large global accounts, and Q1 FY27 is described as secured on price, supply contracts and inventory.
Management expects overall industry demand to be muted in the next year or so, with share gains expected for the company during inflationary periods.
Management said it gained market share in India in the first few weeks of Q4-end, as smaller players hold less inventory buffer.
Flavours margins improved sequentially on rapid volume growth and operating leverage, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Return on the Rs 350 crore capex and Rs 80-85 crore opex in new centres: when will returns come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns will take longer than 1-2 years; new centres break even after about 3 years and markets are 20-25x India in size. Management said it is on track in US and Europe and has no large India capex planned apart from fire-related rebuild.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins normalise to low teens this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, it expects to reach that level quickly, while noting the adjusted EBITDA target is about 13-13.5% for H1.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost is passed on, and how will inventory cycles affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on RM increases under contracts, holds 2-3 months of raw material and sets client prices against stock on hand, reviewing every 2-3 months; it expects no repeat of the past inventory-driven margin lag.

qa_highlights.question: FX impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FX added about 3% to 3.5% to revenue growth in Q4 and FY26; management said revenue transactions are broadly neutral but the dollar loan creates translation pressure on margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the detailed margin roadmap (13% to 17%) not been published, and what is the CCC outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported EBITDA target of about 14% by FY29 stands, but priorities have shifted to quarterly delivery after the March 2026 environment change. Cash conversion cycle is about 140 days and expected to persist until inflation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 35 crore low-margin exit hurt FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, citing strong demand and early indications in the first 45 days of Q1; European growth is expected to accelerate with the Almere plant.

risks_watch: Raw-material and crude-linked cost inflation has not yet fully flowed through; management expects pressure in coming quarters despite pricing actions.
Gross debt is expected to rise in the next 3-6 months due to inventory build, and insurance receipts after the fire may lag capex.
Start-up losses of about Rs 80-85 crore a year from US, UK and Germany development centres continue until revenue ramps (about 3 years).
Supplier contract honouring in flavours and raw material availability over the next 2-3 months.
Management did not give full-year FY27 guidance and deferred the detailed margin roadmap.
539450|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on H1 FY27 margin and pricing visibility, but cautious and non-committal beyond H1 due to raw-material and inflation uncertainty. Management was candid about the Rs 35 crore one-off and the reported margin gap, and it deferred the detailed three-year margin plan.
key_quotes: So, as we have given our guidance and even if you look at the fourth quarter this year, we are at 13% and something adjusted EBITDA from the sustainable operating business.
We believe that we have taken adequate steps to keep close to this number at least for the first half of this year and we will wait and watch and see and take corrective steps as necessary.
Our key objective remains clear, protecting margins while ensuring supply security for our customers.

539450|2026-06.headline: S H Kelkar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore, with EBITDA up 21% to Rs 89 crore and margin at 13.4%.
539450|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to Rs 662 crore and EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 89 crore, with margin expanding to 13.4% from 12.6%. Flavours was the standout, at Rs 112 crore, which management says includes about Rs 15 crore of one-off pre-ordering and stock build; the normalised run-rate is about Rs 95-96 crore. Global Ingredients was softer on supply gaps, and Fragrances India was flat as the company exited low-margin business and repriced clients. Net debt rose Rs 65 crore to Rs 852 crore on inventory build and capex, and a Rs 30 crore insurance exceptional item was booked.

financial_highlights.change: Supported by product mix and raw material planning
Normalised about Rs 95-96 crore excluding about Rs 15 crore pre-ordering
Expected to rise to Rs 38-39 crore per quarter after Vanvate capitalisation

segments.name: Flavours
segments.commentary: Strong broad-based growth; Rs 112 crore in Q1 versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore attributed to pre-ordering and extra channel stock. Management expects Q2 to be above Rs 95-96 crore but not above Rs 112 crore.

segments.name: Fragrances (Europe and international)
segments.commentary: Healthy growth led by Europe and select international markets. Europe plant operational since May; European capex completed. Segment margins are weighed down by higher R&D and global CDC opex.

segments.name: Fragrances India
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, against a strong Q1 FY26 base. Company exited low-margin business and held back shipments until price corrections were agreed; about 95% of clients accepted price increases.

segments.name: Global Ingredients
segments.commentary: Softer quarter on lower demand in select export markets and supply gaps from raw-material constraints; management expects recovery in H2.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for full FY27, but would not give a precise full-year margin range beyond the next 2-3 months.
If double-digit growth holds, EBITDA in absolute terms should be similar to Q1 levels; margin could vary about 1% either way.
Raw material costs said to be fixed for about 6 months via stock in hand and contracts; about 45 days extra inventory built to pass on future cost shocks.
Net debt expected broadly flat at June level through Q2 (may rise slightly in September), then fall about Rs 25 crore per quarter from Q3.

Target ETR below 30%, from 31.5-32% currently.
Long-term targets: ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years and 20% long term; European business ROCE 17-18% over the long run.
US revenue expected at about USD 1.5-2 million for FY27; UK business needs 12-15 months before material revenue.

Quarterly depreciation about Rs 35 crore, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate capitalisation.

Global Ingredients supply curtailed due to raw-material uncertainty; backward integration and China de-risking steps said to be in place.
Unilever and global accounts: ongoing project flow but no large new breakthroughs; Unilever's own pricing pressures and weak India launches noted.
Management cites a US plus UK fragrance market of about USD 10 billion, roughly 4-5x India's fragrance market, with about USD 100 million addressable in the near term.
Around 10-11% of revenue comes from products launched in the last 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year Flavours budget and how much did FX add to revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Flavours was Rs 112 crore versus a normalised Rs 95-96 crore, with about Rs 15 crore pulled forward. Like-for-like growth was about 9%, and FX added about 5 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: Is flat India Fragrance a high-base effect, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 was strong. The company deliberately exited low-margin business, held back shipments during price negotiations, and says it now services almost all clients after building inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be guided for FY27, and is the Q1 gross margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise full-year range was given. Management says Q1 is a normal quarter, not exceptional, so EBITDA should be similar in absolute terms if double-digit growth continues, with margin varying about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the factory timelines, debt path and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Vanvate commissions in Q3. Debt stays near June levels, then falls about Rs 25 crore a quarter from Q3. ETR is 31.5-32% now, targeted below 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe ramp-up and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Germany is expected to break even in FY27 or FY28, the US a year later, and the UK a year after that. Long-term European ROCE is 17-18%, and group ROCE above 15% in 3-5 years, rising to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance claim status and how is depreciation trending?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 30 crore was received in Q1, with Rs 50-60 crore still pending and full settlement expected in FY27. Depreciation is about Rs 35 crore a quarter, rising to Rs 38-39 crore after Vanvate.

539523|2026-03.headline: Alkem Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.6% YoY to INR36,033 million and FY26 EBITDA crossed INR3,000 crore, with management guiding FY27 margins to 20-21%.
539523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR36,033 million (+14.6% YoY), with India sales up 8.8% to INR23,245 million and international sales up 25.4% to INR12,223 million. Q4 EBITDA was INR5,174 million at a 14.4% margin, and FY26 EBITDA grew 32.2% YoY per management, with a 20.4% full-year margin. Q4 net profit was INR2,365 million after exceptional items of INR602.7 million (labour code gratuity/leave liability) and INR747 million (real estate impairment). Management flagged rising logistics, API and packaging costs from geopolitical disruption, and announced that CEO Dr. Vikas Gupta is leaving; a new CEO search is underway.

financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 12.4% in Q4 FY25 (as stated)

financial_highlights.value: INR3,052 million per slide (management also said crossed INR3,000 crore); margin 20.4%
financial_highlights.change: Margin up from 19.4% in FY25; EBITDA +19.6% YoY (stated), +32.2% (stated for Q4 context)

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 India sales grew 8.8% YoY to INR23,245 million; management said branded generics grew close to 10%. IQVIA shows Q4 growth of 11.1% vs IPM ~10%, with chronic +16.1% vs IPM 13.6% and acute +10% vs IPM 7.7%.

segments.name: International (US and ROW)
segments.commentary: Q4 international sales rose 25.4% YoY to INR12,223 million; FY26 international sales were INR4,610 million (+22.5%). Management did not split US and ROW figures for the quarter.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: FY26 trade generics growth was about 4.3% on an annualised basis after the carve-out into a separate entity; management is prioritising margin over top-line.

segments.name: Enzene (CDMO/biologics)
segments.commentary: Enzene India is at a high-teens EBITDA margin; Enzene US is loss-making during ramp-up and the group is not expected to be EBITDA positive this year. US CDMO revenue was under INR100 crore last year.

segments.name: Medtech (Occlutech)
segments.commentary: Medtech contributes less than 1% of revenue today. Occlutech acquisition expected to close in 45-60 days.

US (dollar terms): high single-digit growth on pharma, plus forex gain and new launches; Tolvaptan launch expected around Sep/Oct 2026 with limited competition.

Semaglutide: injectable approved and launched in India in March 2026; oral tablet in clinical trials; US filing planned in about 1.5 years.

Semaglutide launched day 1 in March 2026; about 11% unit market share in the latest IQVIA report.

Domestic field force around 14,500 MRs at group level; attrition 18-19%.
Geopolitical environment has raised logistics, API and packaging costs; management hedges 80% of forex exposure and buys API and packaging inventory on price dips.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for India growth and the margin path given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: India is targeted at 100-150 bps above the market; FY26 margin of 20.4% is the baseline and FY27 is seen at 20-21%, with 100 bps annual expansion now a moving target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech deal timing and the impact on numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Deal expected to close in 45-60 days; if it closes, Q2 FY27 would carry a full quarter impact. Medtech is under 1% of revenue today.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Denosumab biosimilar timeline in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: US approval is possibly by Q1 CY27 subject to inspection; no launch this year. Europe has one partner for the Prolia biosimilar; the Xgeva version has no partner yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CEO succession and CXO plan?
qa_highlights.answer: A new CEO will be hired from top global candidates, taking a few months. Non-pharma group businesses (Occlutech, Enzene) report to other promoters or the MD.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tolvaptan launch and expected contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch expected around September or October 2026 as a limited-player launch, so contribution comes in H2 FY27; base US business faces value erosion.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for dividend and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 25-30% of PAT; absolute payout is expected to be maintained, so the payout percentage will rise after the tax reset. No acquisitions for 12 months.

539523|2026-06.headline: Alkem Q1 FY27 revenue rose close to 11% to INR3,740 crores, but net profit fell 21.7% on tax, and the Daman US plant received an OAI status.
539523|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR3,740 crores, up close to 11% YoY, with India at INR2,497 crores (+10.3%) and international at INR1,222 crores (+16%). EBITDA margin was 20.5% (EBITDA up 3.7% YoY), PBT was up about 1.8%, and net profit fell 21.7%, which management attributed to tax. Trade Generics was flat YoY in April-June, which dragged India growth, while branded generics grew about 12%. The Daman facility received an OAI status from the USFDA, which management says has not interrupted supplies.

segments.name: India formulations - Trade Generics
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; drag due to tighter receivables/DSO practices, API-linked price increases and competition. Management says it is number 1 or 2 in the segment.

segments.name: India formulations - Branded / non-trade (ex-Trade Generics)
segments.commentary: Branded generics grew about 12%; price up about 6%, new launches about 3%, volume about 2%. Chronic grew 17.9% vs IPM 15.4%; acute grew 12.3% vs IPM 10.1%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,222 crores, +16% YoY. Management cites Chile, Australia and small high-growth markets such as Germany (35-40% growth) as drivers.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Management described US as challenging with little volume growth and near-flat price erosion; FY27 US guidance now high single digit to mid, helped by currency. Daman plant supplies about 45% of US revenue.

segments.name: MedTech (Occlutech and ortho)
segments.commentary: Occlutech acquisition completed mid-July, so no Q1 impact; ex-diligence, Q1 EBITDA loss of about INR5-7 crores from ortho/MedTech. FY27 target about INR400 crores sales for the roughly 8.5 months of ownership with breakeven EBITDA.

segments.name: US CDMO (Enzene, mAbs)
segments.commentary: Operating cost about INR60 crores per quarter; breakeven needs about USD25-30 million annualised revenue, now expected in FY28, with capex needed later and no US FDA approval yet on the facility.

539524|2026-03.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16.6% to Rs 703 crore; FY27 guided to early-to-mid-teens growth and 27-28% margins.
539524|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16.6% YoY to Rs 703 crore, driven by sample volume growth of 12.9%, while Q4 EBITDA rose 10.5% to Rs 187 crore at a 26.6% margin. Q4 PAT fell to Rs 132 crore from Rs 156 crore, as last year included a Rs 41 crore one-time benefit and this year had a Rs 30 crore Labour Code charge in Q3. FY26 revenue grew 12.2% to Rs 2,763 crore with a 27.2% EBITDA margin, and the Board approved a final dividend of Rs 4 per share. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to early-to-mid-teens and margins to 27-28%, while stepping up spending on labs, infrastructure and A&P.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited infra upgrades including Delhi NCR and higher A&P spend as geographies expand; FY27 margin guided at 27-28% with investment in labs continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 19% YoY in Q4, and was there a regrouping?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 129 crore vs Rs 108 crore: courier and transport costs were regrouped from employee benefit to other expenses; the rise reflects 14 new labs and Sovaaka operations, not the Labour Code.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 tax rate near 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: A reversal of deferred tax after an income tax assessment and refund; the underlying tax rate is still about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for early-to-mid-teens FY27 growth when the post-COVID run rate was 10-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lab and collection network additions are maturing, Delhi NCR is expected to keep growing at double digits, and Suburban is recovering; the range is 13-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is GLP-1 adding to patient volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth reflects the collection and lab network and that no differential impact from GLP-1 is being ascribed.

qa_highlights.answer: Suburban is no longer reported separately and is part of West; management said West margins still have room to improve, and the company-wide margin is 27-28%.

539524|2026-06.headline: Dr. Lal PathLabs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.1% to Rs 798 crore, with EBITDA margin of 31.0%, and guidance may move toward mid-teens growth.
539524|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 798 crore grew 19.1% YoY, described as the highest quarterly growth in four years, led by patient volume growth of 8.2% and sample volume growth of 10.7%. EBITDA rose 28.7% to Rs 247 crore (31.0% margin) and PAT rose 27.2% to Rs 170 crore. Management said the CGHS/ECHS price revision adds 2-3% to realisations, and it may be more towards mid-teens revenue growth than early teens. Management will not revise the 27-28% margin guidance until after Q2, and leans towards reinvesting any upside.

segments.commentary: B2C is about 75% of the mix and B2B about 25%, which management considers a good balance and intends to keep.

segments.name: Genomics
segments.commentary: Contributes less than 5% of the portfolio and is not yet moving significantly; management does not disclose it separately.

segments.name: West India (Suburban)
segments.commentary: Growth is close to double digits after LIMS integration. Suburban profitability is no longer tracked separately after its voluntary liquidation and back-end merger.

segments.name: Delhi NCR

539551|2026-03.headline: Narayana Q4 FY26: India margin rose to 25.1% (from 21.5%), but consolidated EBITDA dipped to ~20% on UK acquisition costs; management gives no formal guidance.
539551|2026-03.overview: Management highlighted high-end case mix and robotic cardiac volumes (about 100 robotic cardiac cases a month in Bangalore) driving India ARPP and margin gains. 539660|2026-03.headline: Best Agrolife FY26 revenue fell 31% to ₹1,257 crore and PAT dropped to ₹9 crore; Q4 posted a ₹37 crore loss.
539660|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a weak year for Best Agrolife, with consolidated revenue of ₹1,257 crore (down 31% YoY), EBITDA of ₹100 crore (8% margin vs 11%) and PAT of ₹9 crore (1% margin vs 4%). Management blamed adverse weather, elevated distributor inventory, weak dealer liquidity and a March spike in raw material prices, and said it deliberately held back ~₹50–70 crore of low-realisation March sales. Two rounds of price increases were taken in April and May 2026, and inventory fell to ₹651 crore from ₹773 crore in FY25.

Management provisioned about Rs 60 crore (around 20% of sales) for sales returns, and said Q2 should be strong if rains hold, while declining to give full-year guidance. Capex is on hold and the QIP has lapsed with the balance subscription not paid, with a possible new QIP still under discussion.

segments.name: Generic portfolio

segments.name: Branded business

539682|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose to INR218.5 crore with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR29.4 crore; Q4 revenue INR62.6 crore, up 41.9% YoY.
539682|2026-03.overview: Mobavenue AI Tech reported Q4 and FY26 results on a call held 18 May 2026 (transcript filed 25 May 2026). Management framed FY26 as its first full year under new leadership, marked by renaming from Lucent Industries, the 100% acquisition of Mobavenue Media Private Limited, and a INR49.99 crore preferential raise. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT each rose sequentially in every quarter of FY26, and revenue per verified outcome climbed from INR44.99 in Q1 to INR48.44 in Q4. Management gave only directional FY27 commentary, anchored on a "Rule of 50" framework (30%+ revenue growth with 20%+ EBITDA margin).

segments.name: International operations
segments.commentary: International revenue was 11.5% of FY26 revenue. UK operations went live during FY26, and LATAM is being set up; the platform serves brands across 10 countries.

segments.name: Direct vs intermediary clients
segments.commentary: Direct clients contributed 73.9% of FY26 revenue, versus reliance on agencies and resellers for the rest.

segments.name: Platform products (GMP 360)
segments.commentary: PrsmX covers awareness (CTV, footfall, brand safety), SurgeX covers mobile user acquisition, DiscoverX and AmplifiX cover OEM and app discovery, and ResurgeX covers re-engagement and retention. Q4 added features completing PrsmX as an omnichannel awareness DSP.

guidance_outlook: FY27 outlook is directional, not formal guidance. Management expects sequential momentum driven by FY26 drivers: international expansion, AI automation, CTV, video streaming and commerce media.
Long-term Rule of 50 framework: sustained annual revenue growth above 30% with EBITDA margin of 20% and above.

FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India; expand UK and LATAM and evaluate other markets, including selective M&A; scale AI and product innovation through Mobavenue AI Labs.

Management said FY27 growth is in line with organic capability, and M&A will be pursued only for technology or market access. Macro risks (geopolitics, oil prices, inflation) are factored into planning.
capex_capacity: Core decision engine moved from rule-based and traditional ML to a proprietary neural network framework during FY26.
Real-time inference under 15 milliseconds, against an industry benchmark of about 50 milliseconds.
Daily processing of more than 125 crore consented signals, up from 100 crore earlier per the Q&A.
Deep neural networks trained on 50 terabytes of data in about one hour, down from 10 to 12 hours. ML models refresh on near-hourly cycles.
Outcomes delivered: 42.72 million verified outcomes in FY26 across roughly 2.5 billion devices. Headcount exceeded 200 employees.
demand_pricing: Demand strongest in Quick Commerce, Fintech and Retail, per management. Travel was strong in Q1 and Q2 but was hit in Q4 by the post-war slowdown, though domestic travel continues to grow.
Revenue per outcome rose from INR44.99 (Q1) to INR48.44 (Q4), attributed to better monetisation, conversion quality and mix toward premium formats.
Around 80% of revenue comes from retained customers. Active client base is 150+ brands.
Top 10 clients contribute about 25% of revenue and top 50 about 60-65%. Management caps any single client at around 6-7% of revenue.
Brands do not give exclusivity; Mobavenue competes with other programmatic platforms. It positions itself as outcome-based platform rather than agency.

qa_highlights.question: Are acquisitions or strategic partnerships being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is selective on M&A, looking for technology capability or market and customer access. FY27 growth is expected to be in line with organic capability, and any deal would be priced carefully.

qa_highlights.question: How is the technology platform being strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Daily signal processing rose to more than 125 crore from 100 crore earlier. Training time on 50 TB fell to about one hour from 10 to 12 hours, and AI now drives campaign planning and real-time optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customer retention and repeat business trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is strong once clients move beyond pilots. It cited 150 active customers who spend monthly or quarterly, with no quantified churn figure.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals show the strongest demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick Commerce, Fintech and Retail are the top three. Travel was slowed in Q4 by the post-war environment, but domestic travel continues to grow.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 12-24 month strategic priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: Three pillars: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, global expansion (UK and LATAM over the next 12-18 months, with Asia and other developed markets later), and product and IP innovation through Mobavenue AI Labs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the repeat business share, how do renewals and price increases work, and what is client concentration risk?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of revenue comes from retained clients. Pricing improved through higher revenue per outcome, not explicit price-escalation clauses. Top 10 clients are about 25% of revenue and top 50 about 60-65%, with a 6-7% single-client cap.

risks_watch: Quick Commerce and Commerce clients carry higher concentration and may breach the 6-7% single-client cap; management is widening platform use to diversify.
Travel demand softened in Q4 after the post-war environment; management cites geopolitics, oil-price volatility and inflation as macro risks.
Employee costs grew 26.1% QoQ in Q4, and PAT margin dipped to 13.5% in Q4 from 13.4% for the full year.
Supply and data costs are about 60% of revenue; margin depends on sustaining revenue per outcome gains.
Further M&A and international expansion (UK, LATAM) could absorb capital raised in the INR49.99 crore preferential issue.
539682|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 execution and sequential growth, with management describing the results as disciplined, not a single-quarter outcome. Guidance is deliberately soft ("directional, not formal"), and management was evasive on quantified retention, repeat-business share and M&A pipeline. Multiple audio-quality interruptions during the Q&A left some answers only partly addressed.
key_quotes: Our long-term operating philosophy continues to be anchored around what we call, and we introduced in the last call as Rule of 50, targeting a sustained annual revenue growth of over 30% along with EBITDA margin profile of 20% and above.
Our outlook for FY27 remains directional rather than formal guidance for us, consistent with our earlier communication too.
Owning all three layers, meaning every signal improves our prediction, every prediction improves our outcome, every outcome improves our next signal.

539682|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 56.9% YoY to Rs 728 million and PAT rose 95% YoY to Rs 117 million, with EBITDA margin at 21.2%.
539682|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 728 million, up 56.9% YoY and 16.3% QoQ, with growth attributed to direct advertiser demand in Quick Commerce, BFSI, FinTech and Retail and to international expansion through agency and reseller models. EBITDA was Rs 154 million (21.2% margin, up 240 bps YoY) and PAT was Rs 117 million (16.1% margin, up 320 bps YoY). Management highlighted the launch of the Mobavenue Neural Engine, the PiiX Apple-ecosystem product, US entry and Singapore/Philippines operations. Direct clients' share of revenue fell to 65.2% from 73.9% in FY26, which management attributed to the agency/reseller route used for international expansion.

segments.commentary: Make up the remaining ~34.8% of revenue. Management cited agency and reseller models as an accelerator for international growth.

segments.commentary: Contributed 20.7% of revenue, with India as the anchor. Markets referenced include UK (first entered, ramping fastest), Latin America, Philippines, Singapore and US; management expects international share to build gradually over coming years.

segments.commentary: Newly launched in Q1 for Apple Search Ads, custom product pages and ASO; management said revenue contribution is negligible today and it will start in India.

Management said it will maintain a 20%+ EBITDA margin while improving it year on year in basis points.
Expects growth drivers from new geographies and products (US, UK, Apple ecosystem, emerging markets) to become meaningful in the next 12 to 18 months.
Expects a growing share of optimisation decisions to be made by the Neural Engine over the next 12 to 18 months.
FY27 priorities: deepen enterprise and mid-market penetration in India, scale globally on an asset-light outcome-based model, and selective inorganic opportunities.

Balance sheet supported by a FY26 preferential raise (about Rs 50 crore per an analyst's reference); capital prioritised for AI stack, international expansion and selective acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct client share fall from 73.9% to 65.2%, and what is the optimal mix with agency/reseller partners?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift is from the agency/reseller entry route for international markets. It described this as a small-to-medium-term approach and expects the direct advertiser base to return to a normal position over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: What moat protects the Neural Engine from global platforms replicating it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it owns the full stack across all three P3 layers and that proprietary consented signals feed a closed feedback loop, with pricing linked to outcomes. It pointed to rising revenue per outcome as evidence.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is 56.9% growth, and what would normalise it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it optimises for full-year performance and targets 30% growth and 20% EBITDA margin over the long term. It said quarter-to-quarter variation is expected as international markets scale.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 56.9% growth: market or share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said general market growth cannot explain 56.9%. It attributed growth to international markets (UK first, then LatAm, Philippines, US, Singapore) and premium inventory such as streaming, CTV, Apple ecosystem and DOOH.

qa_highlights.question: What is PiiX's revenue contribution and size of opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PiiX revenue is negligible today. It cited Apple's Indian reach at about 6% growing to 8-10%, and said the product will start in India before going international.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential raise proceeds be allocated, and what are the key risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are mainly for strategic acquisitions with disciplined selection, plus technology investment. Named risks were regulation, currency (revenue balanced between INR and USD), AI disruption and inflation; no near-term inflation impact was seen.

risks_watch: Shift in revenue mix toward agency/reseller channels (direct share down to 65.2% from 73.9%) and its effect on margins.
International execution in US, UK, Singapore and Philippines, which management says drives a large share of growth but is still early.

Client concentration: top-5 sectors contribute about 70-80% of revenue, and top-5/top-10 client shares were not disclosed.

539686|2026-03.headline: K.P. Energy FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore (up 57% YoY) and Q4 PAT hit a record INR 78.69 crore.
539686|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR 1,505.54 crore (up 57% YoY), EBITDA of INR 328.44 crore (up 68%) and PAT of INR 181.4 crore (up 57%). Q4 net sales reached an all-time quarterly high of INR 631.81 crore, up 83% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 21% (up 194 bps YoY) and PAT of INR 78.69 crore. The order book is about 2 GW (INR 3,000 plus crore), with about 230 MW added in Q4, while operating cash flow weakened due to higher inventory (WTG turbines) and advances. Management guided to 40-50% growth in FY27.

Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR2,490 crores (+115% YoY, +5% QoQ), net revenue INR149 crores (+11% YoY), and adjusted PAT INR95 crores (+90% YoY). Management said FY27 profitability would not show a "hockey stick" and guided consolidated margins similar to or slightly higher than current levels, with formal FY27 guidance deferred to the Q1 call. Lending was reframed as asset-light, with minority stakes in NBFCs (Ratnaafin, up to 2.5%) and a proposed investment in Online PSB Loans; the company said it will not deploy its balance sheet into lending.

539872|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores and PAT 26.9% to INR14.1 crores, with formulations up 82%.
539872|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores in Q2 FY27 and 6.2% QoQ, with H1 revenue up 15.1% to INR341.5 crores. EBITDA rose 12.2% YoY to INR32.1 crores at an 18.2% margin, while gross margin fell to 48.3% amid West Asia disruption. Formulations (INR41.7 crores, up 82% YoY) and export API (INR62.6 crores, up 28.5%) offset a weaker domestic API line (INR71.6 crores, down from INR76.3 crores). Management reiterated FY29 targets of INR900-1,000 crores revenue and 18-21% EBITDA margin, and flagged higher inventory held as a precaution against Gulf disruption.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR71.6 crores vs INR92 crores in Q1 and INR76.3 crores a year ago; H1 up 10.1% YoY to INR163.9 crores. Management expects little pricing improvement over time.

segments.name: Export API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR62.6 crores, up 28.5% YoY; Magnesium L-Threonate supplied to a US patent holder contributes about 11-12% of total turnover.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crores, up about 82% YoY, driven by the Cenobamate API tablet launch in September through eight marketing partners; formulations are about 24% of revenue in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY29 target: revenue of INR900-1,000 crores with EBITDA margin of 18-21%.
Management said it is on track for the earlier guidance of 10-15% revenue and profit growth with 18-20% margin; Q2 growth was almost 20%.
Operating cash flow expected to be more than INR30 crores for FY27.
Total FY27 capex expected at INR65-80 crores; about INR50-60 crores per year thereafter to reach INR1,000 crores revenue.
Management expects gross margin and EBITDA margin to be maintained in coming quarters, supported by product mix.

Genrx (acquired, NCLT approved): INR200-250 crores revenue potential in two to three years. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after commissioning in Q2 FY28. Peptide facility: first-year revenue INR70-100 crores in FY28-29.
capex_capacity: Peptide manufacturing plant (250 kg per annum, solid-phase synthesis and fermentation) scheduled for completion by 31 March 2027.
Oncology API plant to commence in Q2 FY28.
Dedicated formulation plant at Nashik (solid oral dosage, nasal, oral oncology, nutraceutical, ointment) expected operational in Q1 FY28.
New R&D centre started in August with over 80 staff, planned capacity of 120 chemists; R&D spend raised to about 2.5-3% of revenue.
Genrx acquisition to handle non-Baroda formulation volumes; new molecules to be made at Baroda, which is an approved facility.
demand_pricing: Cenobamate API tablets approved by DCGI (first in India, six strengths), launched commercially in September 2026; repeat orders received from partners, but secondary sales not yet known.

Regulatory filings: 110 DMFs filed, with approvals taking two to three years; 8 CEPs approved and 4 under review in Europe; 17 products registered with KDMF in South Korea; 3 products registered in Egypt with 10 more planned; 17 products identified for Brazil CBPF submission.
API pricing described as under pressure with little prospect of improvement; management said prices are more or less stabilised but volatile given Gulf disputes, freight and interest rates.
Management expects 60-70% of the portfolio to be backward integrated in two to three years.
Mix target over three to four years: formulations 45-50% and API 50-55% (vs about 20-24% formulations today).

qa_highlights.question: Will Manjusar formulation production shift to Genrx, and what is the role of the Nashik facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nashik is a strategic capacity addition for the next two to three years; new molecules will be made at the approved Baroda facility, and Genrx will handle other formulations for different markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital inventory rise and will it normalise by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the higher inventory is a deliberate policy decision to avoid stoppages from the Gulf dispute; management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue potentials from Genrx and the oncology API plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Genrx: INR200-250 crores in two to three years after start-up. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after it is in operation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and is guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR65-80 crores; CFO said the company is on track for the earlier 10-15% growth and 18-20% margin guidance, with Q2 growth near 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given weak H1 conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected above INR30 crores for FY27; Q2 operating cash flow about INR15 crores; receivable days improved from 145 to 135.

qa_highlights.question: How is EBITDA margin holding up despite a roughly 225-250 bp YoY gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed stable EBITDA margin to product mix: export and formulation (Cenobamate launch) offset the domestic API dip, and said margins are expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio can be backward integrated, and what are the margin effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% of products could be backward integrated in two to three years, with revenue from these products rising about 10-15% and margins improving; no specific margin figure was given.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell YoY (about 225-250 bp per analyst) amid West Asia/Gulf disruption, freight and interest-rate pressure; management expects improvement but gave no figure.

Domestic API revenue fell QoQ and YoY in Q2; API prices described as under pressure.

Cenobamate secondary sales not disclosed; management could not quantify FY27/FY28 revenue from it.
Execution risk from several new plants (peptide by March 2027, Nashik Q1 FY28, oncology Q2 FY28) and rapid senior hiring; management cited facilities as the main bottleneck over three years.

539876|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, with EBIT margin exiting near 10% versus 6.8% in H1.
539876|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, led by 10% growth in ECD and 14% growth in lighting. Management said EBIT margin improved from 6.8% in H1 to about 10% in Q4, driven by operating leverage, premiumisation, pricing and cost optimisation. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 271 Cr (11.9% margin). Butterfly returned to double-digit revenue and profit growth, and management took an impairment on its Butterfly carrying value, which is non-cash but hits ROCE and asset turnover. Management also announced a new super-premium product line, Crompton Rhion, and an identical dividend to last year.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, Q4; management called it industry-leading
YoY, Q4, with steady EBIT margins
Management says Butterfly is now cash flow positive

segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 10%, broad-based across pumps, small domestic appliances and fans. Fans saw record March volumes; BLDC portfolio growing 30%-plus. Management says it gained share in every ECD product in FY26 but did not give category numbers.

segments.commentary: Management said FY26 growth was in the early 20s percent and Q4 growth close to 30%, with a step-up in profitability. New launches included infrared cooktops, air fryers and premium juicers.

segments.name: Lighting (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 14%. Government share of B2B mix fell about 500 bps in FY26. Y-o-Y margin said to be roughly flat despite materially higher ad spend in the quarter.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 17% with steady EBIT margins and higher advertising spend. Management says it is back to strong double-digit growth in both revenue and profit, and an impairment was taken on its carrying value.

segments.commentary: Solar pumps revenue was about Rs 200 Cr last year and grew significantly this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr (about 38,000 units in Andhra plus Telangana), with about 5,000 homes installed so far. Management targets a Rs 2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years (corrected from Rs 1,500 Cr).

segments.name: Wires (Crompton Armor)
segments.commentary: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and now selling in South India; national rollout is planned over the year rather than all at once.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margins to recover over time as input-cost turbulence from the war eases, but would not give a timeline.
Management said further material cost inflation came in April; it plans to offset this through pricing and Unnati cost actions, and says some benefits could be back-ended.
Dividend declared identical to last year.
Solar business aspiration: Rs 2,000 Cr over 3-4 years (management corrected the figure from Rs 1,500 Cr).
Butterfly will focus on gaining traction in North, East, West (NEW) markets in the coming year.
Water heater BEE norms from July: management said it is fully prepared, with some cost increase to mitigate or pass on.
capex_capacity: Annual R&D and innovation spend about Rs 100 Cr, per management.
Rhion super-premium PL created; the Large Kitchen Appliance business folds into it; about 70 EBOs already operating.
Lighting supply chain restructured: Baddi unit restructured earlier, Baroda cost base reset with VRS.
Wires rollout ramping from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to other states over the year.
Solar rooftop execution stepped up in the last 2-3 months.
demand_pricing: Two price increases in ECD since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative price increase in fans in FY26, mostly taken in Q4.
Management said cost inflation continued into April; a war room tracks costs weekly or daily.
Butterfly has taken price increases similar to ECD's.
Residential pumps demand was tepid due to heavy rain; management says it held share. Agricultural pumps grew in the teens after product launches.
Air cooler inventory was cleared in the season; management says it gained marginal share. Water heaters were among the top 2 players in GT, now said to be No. 2.
Management says traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY and solar pump collections are on expectation; no stress seen so far in builders or contractors.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases were taken against the cost inflation, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Two ECD price increases since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative in fans in FY26, mostly in Q4, which offset material inflation. Further inflation came in April, and management is waiting to see before deciding pricing for the rest of Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 contribution and FY27 ramp-up from solar pumps and rooftops?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar pumps grew from about Rs 20 Cr three years ago to about Rs 200 Cr last year, and grew strongly again this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr, with about 5,000 homes installed. Management declined to give an FY27 contribution estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins dip, and is growth troughing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins were roughly flat YoY despite higher ad spend. Growth came from a shift away from government B2B contracts (down about 500 bps), a higher-ASP B2C mix (panels, floodlights) and a reset supply chain and cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Butterfly impairment's tax impact and is the merger still planned?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tax angle and it is an accounting impairment, not a write-off. Management said the impairment is unrelated to the merger plan, which remains on the cards at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the national rollout plan for wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, with ramp-up across the country over the year and distribution via the full Crompton network. No specific revenue targets given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there channel or payment stress in the value chain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY, solar pump collections are on track, and FY26 operating cash flow crossed Rs 500 Cr. Management said builder and contractor exposure is small and no stress is seen so far.

Water heater BEE norms from July may add cost and pressure margins in LDA.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of Butterfly growth vs competitor TTK's 34%?

539876|2026-09.headline: Crompton Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA 24.1% to Rs 205 Cr, with margin up 40 bps to 9%.
539876|2026-09.overview: Crompton delivered its third straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, with all business segments growing double digits per management. Revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA rose 24.1% YoY to Rs 205 Cr at a 9% margin. PBT excluding exceptional items grew 36.2%; the prior-year quarter carried a Rs 20 Cr Baroda plant restructuring exceptional, which inflates reported PAT growth of 65%. Management said price increases of about 80% of cost inflation have been passed through, supply disruptions from Q1 are over, and inventory days are back to year-ago levels. E-commerce was subdued due to a channel repositioning, and A&P spend was lower in H1.

financial_highlights.metric: Exceptional item (prior year, Baroda plant restructuring)

financial_highlights.change: Historical run-rate Rs 250-260 Cr per year

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables: fans, pumps, appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY with EBIT margin up YoY to 11.6%; BLDC fans grew about 40% in general trade. SDA grew over 20%, and LDA grew at double digits led by water heaters.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 298 Cr, up 14.3% YoY, driven by B2C ceiling and outdoor lights and B2B industrial and indoor commercial. EBIT margin 12.9%, lower YoY due to pre-contracted B2B orders.

segments.name: Butterfly
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15.9% YoY excluding an in-house mixer grinder sale in the base; growth was largely price-led. Management said the core business grew about 16%.

segments.name: Solar pumps
segments.commentary: Slowed as Kusum 1.1 order inflow tapered; management expects a pickup after Kusum 2.0 is announced. More than 50% of the AP government order book has been executed.

segments.name: Solar rooftop and wires
segments.commentary: Solar rooftop (B2C and C&I) is live in six to seven states; wires launched in South India in Q1 and extended to Punjab, Delhi NCR and Gujarat. Management described both as nascent.

segments.name: LKA and Rhion
segments.commentary: Restructured under Butterfly CBO Shweta Sagar, to leverage the Butterfly ecosystem. Management cited a prior EBITDA loss of Rs 16-25 Cr for the business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew more than 70% YoY to a record quarterly revenue, led by fans with pumps, LDA and SDA also exported; markets are Africa, Middle East and South Asia. Margins are slightly lower than domestic, but sales are on cash terms.

guidance_outlook: Management says the company is on track for its medium-term guidance and expects double-digit revenue and profit growth to continue over the coming quarters.
Long-term EBITDA margin ambition of 11-12% by FY29, as stated in the investor deck; management said this is on a larger revenue base.
New businesses are targeted at 14-15% of revenue in the long run; they were about 10% of revenue in Q2 FY27 per the call.
Solar rooftop order execution is expected to complete in the next quarter, with some spillover after that.
A&P spend is expected to stay broadly at last year's absolute level, subject to macro conditions.
Fans are targeted at 1.5-1.7x category growth, per the investor day.
capex_capacity: Evaluation of a greenfield manufacturing plant is at an advanced stage, to add capacity in fans, appliances and wires.
Pumps and most new businesses (solar pumps, solar rooftop, wires, LKA) are outsourced; the company has not yet committed to in-house manufacturing.
Management said there is no supply constraint today.
Solar rooftop installation is done through an agency partner on the company's behalf.
New businesses leverage existing go-to-market and supply chain, so no separate sales teams or fresh cost centres are planned.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price increases of 11-15% across most non-lighting businesses over the last six months, and about 15-16% in some; fans cumulatively about 17-18% over nine months.
About 80% of cost inflation has been passed through; the remainder is being covered by Unnati cost savings and operating leverage.
Q2 was the first quarter in which price increases were largely passed on with positive volume growth across categories, per management.
General trade (about 80% of business) and rural both grew double digits; e-commerce was subdued after a deliberate channel repositioning.
Competitors have announced price increases, but management said these have not always been implemented.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been passed on, and what more is needed for Q3 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price increases were 11-15% across businesses excluding lighting, and about 80% of cost increases have been passed on. Further increases will follow as commodities move.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar rooftop revenue was recognised in Q1, and how much of the order remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a percentage split. About half the order has been executed across Q1 and Q2; most of the remainder is expected to complete next quarter, with some spillover.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fan pricing lower than the overall price-hike number?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said the 15% figure refers to cumulative price increases over the last two quarters, with fans at the top of the range. Fans cumulatively rose about 17-18% over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Solar rooftop margin structure: is installation cost borne by Crompton?
qa_highlights.answer: Crompton sells a turnkey product at about Rs 1.8 lakh for a 3 kW unit, with installation included. An agency partner performs the installation on Crompton's behalf, so the cost sits between gross margin and EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did A&P spend fall as a share of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower e-commerce promotion spend from channel repositioning, and brand relaunch costs booked outside A&P. H1 A&P was about Rs 100 Cr against a Rs 250-260 Cr annual run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin ambition of 11-12% by FY29 a margin recovery or expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 11-12% is a recovery to the FY25 level of 11.8%, with operating leverage coming on a higher revenue base as growth is raised about 2.5x from the phase-one average of about 6%.

risks_watch: Commodity cost volatility and geopolitics; about 20% of cost inflation is still unrecovered.
Solar pump order inflow remains lumpy until Kusum 2.0 orders come through.
Lighting B2B margin pressure from pre-contracted orders.
E-commerce revenue remains subdued during the channel repositioning.
A&P comparability and the classification of brand relaunch spend outside A&P.
Solar rooftop profitability depends on the agency installation model and selective government tendering.

rows.label: Kusum 2.0 solar pump order pickup
rows.why: Solar pump orders slowed as Kusum 1.1 tapered and management expects a pickup after Kusum 2.0 is announced; more than 50% of the AP government order book is already executed.

rows.label: Solar rooftop order completion
rows.why: About half of the solar rooftop order was executed across Q1 and Q2 and most of the remainder is expected to complete next quarter, with some spillover.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum, price pass-through and the FY29 11-12% margin ambition, but cautious on unpredictable commodity costs, and evasive on fan volume drivers and solar rooftop revenue recognition; analysts probed pricing, A&P classification and the solar rooftop margin stru

539889|2026-03.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q4 FY26: gross margin rose to 28% from 25.9% in Q3, but EBITDA margin slipped to about 8.1% and core-category volumes fell 3%.
539889|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue crossed INR3,800 crores with 5% volume growth, and the new-age business (Avvatar and Pride of Cows) grew 91% for the year. Q4 gross margin improved to 28% (25.9% in Q3, 26.7% a year earlier) on mix and pricing, but employee costs jumped on one-offs and EBITDA margin dipped to about 8.1%. Q4 branded volumes fell about 5% and core-category volumes about 3%, which management attributed to a weak export and institutional base effect. Management guided only qualitatively: double-digit core volume growth as the aspiration, and a move to double-digit EBITDA margin over coming years.

financial_highlights.metric: New-age business revenue (Avvatar + Pride of Cows)
financial_highlights.value: over INR100 crores in Q4 (second straight quarter); about INR360 crores base cited by analyst
financial_highlights.change: over 100% YoY in Q4; 91% for FY26
vs 25.9% in Q3 FY26; 26.7% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: down about 5% YoY (core categories down about 3%)
about INR9 crores increase, from INR6 crores to about INR15 crores

financial_highlights.change: up about INR150 crores, attributed to rate variance (management says quantity variance nil)

segments.name: Core categories (Ghee, Cheese, Paneer)
segments.commentary: About 60% of business. Q4 volume down about 3%, due to lower export and institutional sales in the base quarter; YTD December volume growth was 12%. Management says Ghee is number 1 with about 22% market share; cheese about 35%.

segments.name: New-age (Avvatar, Pride of Cows)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crores quarterly revenue for the second quarter running (INR102 crores prior quarter, INR100 crores in Q4), with revenue growing over 100% YoY in Q4. Pricing and promotion changes in Q4 created a transitional gap. Pride of Cows price raised from INR120 to INR135 per litre.

segments.name: Avvatar protein / sports nutrition
segments.commentary: Management estimates a 14-15% share of the protein segment on quick commerce and marketplaces only. About 65% of Avvatar sales come via e-commerce, per an analyst.

guidance_outlook: New-age share of revenue targeted at 20-25% in 3-5 years; management equates this to about INR1,000 crores within the INR10,000 crores ambition, but declined to give a FY29 number.
Capex guidance for FY27 of INR60-70 crores (FY26 spend about INR100 crores).
Aspiration of double-digit core-category volume growth; no formal FY27 guidance given.
Aspiration to move EBITDA margin to double digits in coming years (FY26 about 8.1%).
Gross margin expected to hold around 27-28%, subject to commodity inflation.
Milk prices expected to stay around INR42/litre for the next 2-3 months, then possibly soften after the monsoon if energy prices stay stable.
Full-year incentive income to fall marginally further from INR46 crores; quarterly sustainable employee cost about INR45-46 crores less about INR7.5-8 crores exceptional items.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to rise from 60 to 80 metric tons, then aiming for 120 metric tons through adjacency capex, not greenfield. Combined ghee and cheese capacity cited at about 110 metric tons.
Capex in FY26 about INR100 crores, mainly cheese expansion and lactose-to-whey improvement; some longer-gestation projects still pending.
Cold chain, warehousing and supply chain in North and South India described as already in place.
Dubai subsidiary: bank account opened in Q4 FY26, but first ODI not yet made; company-owned depot on hold for 2-3 months due to Middle East conflict.
demand_pricing: Q4 price increases taken on Ghee, liquid milk, Pride of Cows and Avvatar; management says gross profit growth has outpaced volume growth, indicating pricing power.
Management attributes the core volume decline to export and institutional sales in the base quarter and says ghee premium is intact.
Milk price inflation of 15% YoY passed on in a calibrated way; packaging cost up on polymer price inflation, which led to milk pouch price increases.
Q3 gross margin was hit by GST-driven price reductions (GST on core categories cut from 12% to 5%).
Whey prices rose sharply; management says whey pricing is driven by milk price volatility rather than global protein prices.
Management claims about 30,000 new general-trade outlets added every quarter, and aims to double SKU depth in existing outlets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the New-age business growth aspirations, and is a separate listing or valuation carve-out of Avvatar being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% of revenue from new-age in 3-5 years, but says it has never considered carving out Avvatar, citing an integrated farm-to-brand model.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new-age revenue been flat QoQ at about INR100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 saw promotions withdrawn on Pride of Cows, a price transition on Avvatar and a channel change, which created a transitional gap. Management expects growth from the INR100 crores base without giving a number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 employee cost jump and the sustainable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: One-offs included about INR9 crores of higher executive director pay (from INR6 crores to about INR15 crores), about INR5 crores of ESOP costs, appraisals and new business heads. Management said about INR7.5-8 crores are exceptional, leaving a regular quarterly run rate of about INR45-46 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core volume growth fall so sharply in Q4 and is there market share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Q4 branded volume fell about 5% and core about 3%, due to a low export base; it denied share loss and reiterated double-digit core volume growth as the aspiration.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin gains flow through to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sequential gross margin rose from about 26% when milk was INR40 to 28% at INR42, and expects to reach double-digit EBITDA over coming years, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the INR730 crore inventory increase?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crores of the increase is rate variance from inflation; quantity variance is nil, and powder inventory is expected to fall as that business shrinks.

risks_watch: Core-category volume trend: Q4 core volume down 3%, and management's double-digit core growth target has not yet been shown in results.
EBITDA margin compression (about 8.1%) despite gross margin gains; employee cost growth above 20% YoY.
Milk and energy price inflation, El Nino and fuel-driven packaging and logistics cost increases; management expects milk to stay at INR42 for 2-3 months.
Lower incentive income (INR46 crores vs INR88 crores) reduces other income support.
Inventory at about INR730 crores, with a rate-driven increase of about INR150 crores.
New-age momentum: Q4 flat QoQ at about INR100 crores; Avvatar e-commerce dependence (about 65%).
Middle East disruption delaying the Dubai depot and international expansion.

539889|2026-06.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.
539889|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached a record INR945 crores, up 11% YoY in value and 3% in volume. EBITDA grew 6% to INR70 crores, with margin down 30 bps to 7.4%; PBT was broadly flat and PAT fell 20% on higher current tax. Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi; 61% of revenue) saw volume fall 2% YoY, with B2C growing and B2B declining modestly; new-age business (Pride of Cows and Avvatar) grew 59% and reached about 13% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; gross margin stable (27.3% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 per call)

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi)
segments.commentary: 61% of Q1 revenue; volume down 2% YoY on transient slowdown in certain channels, value up 10%. B2C grew strongly while B2B declined modestly; B2C flagship growth was 'high single digit to close to double digit'. Dahi now included in flagship (previously in Others).

segments.name: New-age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Grew 59% YoY, about 13% of revenue vs 9% a year earlier. Portfolio expanded into protein bars, ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee with 15 g protein per serving (launched Q1), creatine. Management said new-age margins are roughly double the company average, without giving a figure.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Down 46% YoY per analyst question; management said this reflects PSI and state incentive income falling after GST cut on ghee and cheese from 12% to 5% in September 2025, plus dahi moving into flagship. UHT and beverages performed reasonably well.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth above 10%, with Q2 and Q3 supported by festive demand.
Calibrated price increases will continue in response to commodity costs; ghee prices were raised late in Q1 and new-age prices were revisited recently.
Milk prices described as stable; slight increase possible in coming months due to monsoon-linked seasonality and festive demand.
Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.
Management aspires to return flagship B2C growth to double digits; B2B will be pursued where margins allow.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to double from 60 to 120 metric tons per day over about 1.5 years, targeted by March 2028.
Doubling cheese capacity to be paired with a parallel expansion in whey protein generation; milk procurement to be scaled up to match.
Renewable energy: a solar JV with Tata Power Solar; biogas power from farm (about 5,000 cattle); the investment value was INR4.6 crores per the annual report, not INR50 crores.
demand_pricing: Whey protein prices reportedly moved from about INR2,500/kg to about INR3,400/kg recently; management said global whey demand is structural, not temporary.
Management said Avvatar retail prices rose only in stages, not 100% as an analyst suggested; consumers switch between protein formats as prices change.
Q1 B2B volumes were deliberately forgone where customers negotiated hard on pricing, to protect margins.
Avvatar sales are 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce and website, and 25% via traditional retail and specialised protein outlets.
Management said Google searches and website traffic rose about 200% over the last two months, after the India's Got Latent association.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth break the roughly 10% sales growth band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will exceed 10%, with Q2 and Q3 festive quarters expected to drive it; Q1 is seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is Avvatar up 59% when retail prices reportedly doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume also grew strongly and that prices rose in stages, not 100%; new products and lower-cost protein entry formats contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin flat despite mix improvement and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said milk cost pass-through was complete in Q1 at INR42/litre, and the mix gain was offset by milk inflation; gross profit growth matched revenue growth at 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are core-category volumes falling despite wider distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is in B2B, where volumes were given up to protect profitability; B2C is not declining.

qa_highlights.question: Can B2B channel losses be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers or channels or give numbers, citing commercial sensitivity; B2B deals are short-term and come and go.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Samay Raina / India's Got Latent deal's cost and ROI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost, timeline or ROI, calling it a special commercial deal aimed at awareness.

qa_highlights.question: Is Avvatar's whey price rise a margin hit given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost of production per kg or margin impact by product, saying margins are reported on a blended basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income spike in alternate quarters?

539957|2026-03.headline: MGL Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR132 crore from INR202 crore QoQ as West Asia LNG disruption curtailed industrial supply to about 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BFSI lagging, what is the Manufacturing margin profile versus BFSI, and what share of contracts is fixed vs variable markup?
qa_highlights.answer: BFSI recovery will take time given outsourcing regulation; Manufacturing PAPM is Rs 800-1,100 vs Rs 600-700 for GS overall. GS contracts are about 70:30 fixed to variable, with about 38% of Q1 new contracts variable.

qa_highlights.question: Is GCC hiring normalising, and is Rs 30 crore quarterly EBITDA (about 11.5-12%) achievable in Professional Staffing? What is steady-state GS margin ex the Rs 176 crore?

GS margin would be a little over 1.5% after normalising for the Labor Code pass-through and April merit cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Labor Code impact going forward and will it recur YoY?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ambition of reaching 1 million associates by 2030, and what role does M&A play?

qa_highlights.question: How does Quess 2.0 economics compare with existing overseas and PS businesses, and what is the dollar-linked revenue base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give margin numbers before MSAs and delivery start; GCC revenue is about Rs 1.5-2.5 lakh per associate per month. Dollar-linked revenue is about 7% today.

EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.

Q3 and Q4 expected to be sequentially better than Q1; management aims for FY28 to be a stronger growth year.

Top BFSI client consolidating from 50+ vendors to about five; LTM is one of the five. Productivity headwinds already absorbed; about 60% of productivity headwinds passed to customers.
Traditional large deals are being fought at price points management called unmanageable; AI rate cards priced higher than traditional rate cards.

Management says about 60-70% of the portfolio has completed the big-client deflation cycle; the remaining 20-30% goes through renewal and consolidation cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seasonal Tech decline recurring every year, and what is the Saudi effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech decline reflects the annual renewal cycle of the top tech account (fiscal starting July) plus Saudi business routed through a JV with a tech company. Management expects Tech to return to normal growth from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will TCV become less relevant, and will LTM disclose ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI deals are shorter and faster to revenue, so TCV understates them. ACV disclosure is planned but deferred by about one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach high-single or double digits by FY28, and is FY27 close to FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 lost about 0.6-0.7% of growth to Saudi, expects H2 better than H1, and aims for FY28 as the stronger year; FY27 growth near FY26 is an endeavour, not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top BFSI client's vendor spend cut a medium-term risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidation from 50+ vendors to five is a multi-year benefit to LTM, with productivity headwinds already passed through in Q3-Q4 of last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payout low versus peers, and what are capital allocation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said payout rose to about 45% from about 40%; reinvestment via M&A and organic investment (BlueVerse, GCC, talent) is prioritised. M&A is open but must be white-space and fairly priced.

qa_highlights.question: Has the macro or pricing environment changed?

TCV and order inflow visibility: deal mix shift to short-tenure AI deals makes TCV less comparable; ACV disclosure is pending.

540025|2026-03.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 2,034 million, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin steady at 31%.
540025|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR 2,034 million (+22% YoY, +18% QoQ) and FY26 revenue reached INR 7,458 million (+17%), both record levels per management. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to INR 632 million at a 31% margin, and PAT rose 69% YoY to INR 453 million (22% margin). Human Healthcare, Animal Healthcare, Bioprocessing and Specialized Manufacturing all grew on a YoY basis, with Serratiopeptidase volumes a key driver. Management flagged input cost inflation (fuel, salt, solvents, packaging, logistics) and a challenging US market, and guided to steady margins and a double-digit growth aspiration for FY27 without quantified guidance.

Anti-inflammatory enzyme EU novel food approval expected this year; management says it could give exclusivity for 5-10 years but no numbers given.

R&D capex planned at about INR 50 crore in FY27 within a total of about INR 130 crore cited on the call.
demand_pricing: Pricing for the Indian Serratiopeptidase business described as broadly constant; growth was volume-driven, with price increases planned to pass on costs from the new year.
Gross margin moderated QoQ; management attributed this to product mix (higher domestic share) and cost inflation, offset by productivity gains and operating leverage.

US business: market shifting toward registration and studies; revenue down about 11% YoY in INR in Q4 per analyst's calculation. Management says growth will be modest, with US demand under pressure from discretionary spending.
Tariffs: company absorbing about 10% of tariff cost for now and passing on gradually; no full pass-through.
Serratiopeptidase: YTD growth about 45% and QoQ about 54%, shared for the last time, per management.
Top product (anti-inflammatory enzyme) 23% of FY26 revenue; top 10 customers 23% of revenue vs 22% in FY25.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited variable vs fixed cost mix and productivity gains on some products, with inflation partly offsetting; no quantified gross margin figure was given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Is there price increase in Indian Serratiopeptidase or only volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is more or less constant and growth is volume-driven; cost pass-through is planned from the new year.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening with US revenue, and should strategy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Market is shifting to registration and studies; strategy is changing accordingly. Management expects US growth in FY27, though 'very challenging'.

qa_highlights.question: Biocatalysis revenue for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 biocatalysis revenue of INR 247 million vs INR 174 million in FY25; no Q4 figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and buyback given INR 700 crore cash and no interim dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the board will evaluate options, including buyback, and decide at the right time; no decision announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating leverage not lifted gross margin from the 75% level seen post-COVID?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose customer traction over margin for now, and expects margins to stay around current levels.

540025|2026-06.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 1,898 million, but EBITDA fell 10% to INR 510 million as margin dropped to 27%.
540025|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 1,898 million grew 2% YoY but fell 7% QoQ, held back by an extra INR 100 million sales reversal for export shipments still in transit. EBITDA declined 10% YoY and 19% QoQ to INR 510 million, with margin at 27% versus 30% a year ago, attributed to lower realisation, higher power and fuel costs, and a sales-mix shift. PAT was INR 386 million, down 5% YoY. Management guided to a return to about 30-32% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth for the rest of the year, and announced a INR 697 million buyback and full acquisition of JC Biotech.
